# SESSION.md — Question 2: complete terminal-agent session export

Each session is embedded below as its unmodified OpenCode JSON export inside a fenced code block. Exports were produced with `opencode session export <session-id>` (OpenCode v2.1.4, 2026-11-03; the lead session was re-exported at finalization, 2026-11-03, to include the final verification work), **not** with `--sanitize`, after an automated secret scan of the raw JSON found no credentials (matches were the substring `sk-` inside `risk-neutral`, plus token counters and the text of the secret-scan commands themselves). Skills: root finding, constrained least squares, no-arbitrage analysis, optimization.\n111: \n112: ### 3.1 Data (public, verified)\n113: \n114: | Item | Source |\n115: |---|---|\n116: | Option chains: strikes, expiries, call/put, contract unit (SSE 50ETF `510050`, 300ETF `510300`, 500ETF, 科创50) | `ak.option_current_day_sse()` |\n117: | Per-contract daily OHLCV, CFFEX CSI 300 index options (`io`), historical | `ak.option_cffex_hs300_daily_sina(symbol=...)`, contract list via `ak.option_cffex_hs300_list_sina()` |\n118: | Underlying index / ETF daily history | `ak.index_zh_a_hist`, `ak.fund_etf_hist_em` |\n119: | Discount curve: SHIBOR (all tenors), LPR, FR007 swap | `ak.macro_china_shibor_all()`, `ak.macro_china_lpr()`, `ak.macro_china_swap_rate()` |\n120: \n121: Single-currency market: the only rate required is domestic; interpolate the SHIBOR zero curve to option tenors. ETF dividend yield: estimate or set to zero, justify. Snapshot: one month of daily chains for ≥ 4 expiries, ≥ 5 sample dates spread over ≥ 2 years.\n122: \n123: ### 3.2 Common requirements\n124: \n125: - Put–call parity residuals $C - P - (S_0 - K e^{-rT})$ per strike; quote filtering rule stated and justified (volume, spread, moneyness band).\n126: - Implied volatility by inverting Black–Scholes:\n127:   $d_\\pm = \\frac{\\ln(F/K) \\pm \\frac12\\sigma^2 T}{\\sigma\\sqrt T}$, $\\ C_{BS}(\\sigma) = e^{-rT}(F N(d_+) - K N(d_-))$;\n128:   solve $C_{BS}(\\sigma_{IV}) = C_{mkt}$ by bracketed Brent on $\\sigma \\in [10^{-4}, 5]$ (both quotes per strike; report divergence cases).\n129: - Deliverable surface: $\\sigma_{IV}(K, T)$ on a fixed log-moneyness grid $k = \\ln(K/F_T)$ per expiry.\n130: \n131: ### 3.3 Option A — Market pipeline (classical)\n132: \n133: 1. Per expiry $T_j$, fit **SVI** in total variance $w(k) = \\sigma_{IV}^2 T$:\n134:    $w(k) = a + b\\big(\\rho(k - m) + \\sqrt{(k-m)^2 + \\eta^2}\\big)$, parameters constrained $b \\ge 0$, $|\\rho| < 1$, $\\eta > 0$; least squares over liquid strikes; report initial values and solver.\n135: 2. No-arbitrage verification, reported per expiry and per date:\n136:    butterfly (Gatheral): $g(k) = \\Big(1 - \\frac{k\\,w'(k)}{2w(k)}\\Big)^2 - \\frac{w'(k)^2}{4}\\Big(\\frac{1}{w(k)} + \\frac14\\Big) \\ge 0$;\n137:    calendar: $w_{T_2}(k) \\ge w_{T_1}(k)$ for $T_2 > T_1$; violations counted and located, not silently dropped.\n138: 3. Term structure: interpolate $w(k, T)$ linearly in total variance; report any negative forward variance.\n139: 4. Repricing consistency: $\\max_k |C_{BS}(\\sigma_{fit}(k)) - C_{mkt}| / C_{mkt}$ on liquid strikes; median and 95th percentile across dates.\n140: \n141: ### 3.4 Option B — Differentiable calibration (PyTorch)\n142: \n143: 1. SVI calibration by gradient descent in `torch` (Adam/L-BFGS), same constraints via reparametrization; convergence profiles vs. `scipy.optimize.least_squares` (iterations to tolerance, wall time, objective value).\n144: 2. Neural surface: $\\hat\\sigma_\\theta(k, T)$ MLP ($\\le 4$ layers), loss = squared pricing error in **option price space** $|C_{BS}(\\hat\\sigma) - C_{mkt}|^2$ plus arbitrage penalties $\\lambda_1 \\max(0, -g(k))^2 + \\lambda_2 \\max(0, -\\partial_T w)^2$; ablation on $(\\lambda_1, \\lambda_2)$.\n145: 3. Robustness study: randomly drop 30% of quotes; compare SVI refit vs. neural surface extrapolation error.\n146: 4. Same verification duties as §3.3.2.\n147: \n148: ### 3.5 Benchmarks (indicative)\n149: \n150: Median liquid-strike repricing relative error < 2%; zero butterfly violations on interior grid after fitting; calibration table across all sample dates.\n151: \n152: ---\n153: \n154: ## 4. Question 2 — Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures\n155: \n156: Course mapping: Sessions 1–2 (BS, Monte Carlo, RNG), Session 4 (profiling). Skills: exact simulation, variance reduction, Greeks, stochastic optimization.\n157: \n158: ### 4.1 Data\n159: \n160: | Item | Source |\n161: |---|---|\n162: | CSI 300 futures (`IF`) and commodity futures daily series (e.g. rebar `RB`, copper `CU`, crude `SC`) | FastboxData read-only (credentials via env) or `ak.futures_main_sina(symbol=...)`, `ak.futures_zh_daily_sina` |\n163: | Underlying index daily history | `ak.index_zh_a_hist` |\n164: | Risk-free curve | SHIBOR (`ak.macro_china_shibor_all`) |\n165: \n166: Calibration set: ≥ 5 years of daily data; estimate $\\hat\\mu, \\hat\\sigma$ (realized vol, log-return regression) per underlying; state the estimation window. Discounting at the interpolated SHIBOR curve.\n167: \n168: ### 4.2 Common requirements\n169: \n170: Exact GBM simulation under $\\mathbb{Q}$: $S_{t_{i+1}} = S_{t_i}\\exp\\big((r - \\tfrac12\\sigma^2)\\Delta t + \\sigma\\sqrt{\\Delta t}\\, Z_i\\big)$, $Z_i \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ i.i.d., seeded generator; $m \\ge 252$ steps/year. Validation duty: European MC price within $3\\times$ standard error of the Black–Scholes closed form (report $z$-score).\n171: \n172: Payoffs (all priced for both MC engines): arithmetic Asian call $A_T = \\frac1m \\sum_i S_{t_i}$; up-and-out call (discrete monitoring, barrier $B$); digital call.\n173: \n174: ### 4.3 Option A — Engine, variance reduction, Greeks, performance\n175: \n176: 1. Naive MC; **antithetic** ($Z, -Z$ pairs; variance ratio reported); **control variate** with the geometric-Asian closed-form price:\n177:    $\\hat\\mu_{CV} = \\hat\\mu_{A} - \\hat\\beta(\\hat\\mu_{G} - \\mathbb{E}[G])$, $\\hat\\beta = \\widehat{\\mathrm{Cov}}(A, G)/\\widehat{\\mathrm{Var}}(G)$.\n178: 2. Greeks: delta and vega by (i) pathwise estimator (e.g. $\\delta = e^{-rT}\\,\\mathbb{E}[\\mathbf{1}_{S_T > K} S_T / S_0]$ for vanilla), (ii) central finite differences with bump $h \\in \\{10^{-1}, 10^{-2}, 10^{-3}\\} S_0$; report bias–variance tradeoff.\n179: 3. Convergence: RMSE vs. $N$ on log–log, all estimators; verify $O(N^{-1/2})$ slope.\n180: 4. Performance: vectorized `numpy` engine vs. naive loop implementation; `timeit` before/after; profiling of the hot loop (line_profiler or equivalent) included in the report.\n181: \n182: ### 4.4 Option B — Deep hedging (PyTorch)\n183: \n184: 1. Simulator as §4.2 with proportional transaction cost $\\kappa$.\n185: 2. Hedging strategy: $\\Delta_t^{\\theta} = f_{\\theta}(S_t/S_{t_0}, t)$, MLP ($\\le 3$ hidden layers); terminal P&L\n186:    $V_T = \\sum_{t} e^{r(T-t)}\\Delta_{t}(S_{t+\\Delta t} - S_t) - \\kappa\\sum_t |\\Delta_t - \\Delta_{t-1}| S_t - \\text{option payoff}$.\n187: 3. Objective: minimize CVaR$_\\alpha$ of $-V_T$ (empirical $\\alpha = 0.95$ quantile-based loss), train on simulated paths (≥ $2^{17}$), validate on independent seeds.\n188: 4. Benchmarks: Black–Scholes delta hedging at rebalancing frequencies $\\{1, 5, 21\\}$ days and cost levels $\\kappa \\in \\{0, 10, 50\\}$ bp; report CVaR$_\\alpha$, variance, expected P&L tables; sensitivity of the learned strategy to $\\kappa$.\n189: \n190: ### 4.5 Benchmarks (indicative)\n191: \n192: Naive-vs-control-variate variance reduction factor ≥ 5 on the Asian payoff; pathwise/finite-difference delta agreement within reported standard errors.\n193: \n194: ---\n195: \n196: ## 5. Question 3 — China macro panel: regimes, nowcasting, indicator clustering\n197: \n198: Course mapping: Sessions 2–3 (pandas, datetime, clustering, SQL), Session 3 KMeans. Skills: panel construction with publication lags, factor models, classification, hierarchical clustering, honest temporal validation.\n199: \n200: ### 5.1 Data (public, verified)\n201: \n202: | Item | Source |\n203: |---|---|\n204: | 170 `macro_china_*` interfaces: GDP, CPI, PPI, PMI (NBS & Caixin), M0/M1/M2, 社融 (TSF), LPR, Shibor, retail sales, industrial output, industrial profits, exports/imports YoY, trade balance, consumer confidence, electricity output, … | `akshare` `macro_china` family |\n205: | Offline fallback | committed snapshot `data/clean/macro_panel.csv` |\n206: \n207: Build a monthly panel $x_{i,t}$, $i = 1,\\dots,d \\ge 20$, ≥ 10 years, with per-series publication lag $L_i$ documented in `metadata.json`. Information set discipline:\n208: $\\mathcal{F}_t = \\{x_{i,s} : s + L_i \\le t\\}$; any use of $x_{i,s}$ with $s + L_i > t$ is leakage and a grading fault.\n209: \n210: ### 5.2 Common requirements\n211: \n212: - Panel hygiene: missing-value report; outlier rule (e.g. MAD) stated; transformations (logs, YoY, Sa) documented per series; standardized panel $\\tilde x_{i,t} = (x_{i,t} - \\mu_i)/s_i$ with statistics from training windows only.\n213: - Regime label: contraction indicator $d_t = \\mathbf{1}\\{\\text{PMI}_{t} < 50 \\text{ and } \\text{PMI}_{t-1} < 50\\}$ (state and justify the labeling; sensitivity to the 49.5 threshold reported).\n214: - Validation: expanding-window walk-forward; metrics: Brier score, AUC, accuracy; naive prior-frequency baseline reported alongside.\n215: \n216: ### 5.3 Option A — Classical\n217: \n218: 1. Factor model: PCA on $\\tilde x_t$; choose rank $r$ by cross-validated nowcast error; $\\tilde x_t = \\Lambda f_t + \\varepsilon_t$.\n219: 2. Nowcasting bridge: $\\hat y_{t} = \\beta_0 + \\beta^\\top f_t$ for quarterly GDP growth (or monthly industrial output), estimated on $\\mathcal{F}_{t}$ only; nowcast revision path within the quarter reported.\n220: 3. Regime model: probit $\\mathbb{P}(d_{t+1} = 1) = \\Phi(\\beta^\\top z_t)$, $z_t$ = factors + yield/spread controls; coefficient table with standard errors.\n221: 4. Indicator clustering: distance $d_{ij} = \\sqrt{2(1 - \\rho_{ij})}$ on rolling 3-year correlations, Ward linkage; dendrogram; cluster stability via adjusted Rand index across adjacent windows; relate clusters to lead/lag cross-correlations with GDP.\n222: \n223: ### 5.4 Option B — Sequence learning (PyTorch)\n224: \n225: 1. Sequence model (LSTM/GRU, ≤ 2 layers, dropout reported): input = window of $\\tilde x_{t-h:t}$, output $\\mathbb{P}(d_{t+1}=1)$; class imbalance handled explicitly (weighting or threshold selection on validation).\n226: 2. Latent macro states: hidden-state embeddings $h_t$; $k$-means on $\\{h_t\\}$; compare clusters with the Option-A correlation clusters (ARI/NMI) and with the regime labels.\n227: 3. Comparison: Brier/AUC of (i) probit baseline, (ii) LSTM, (iii) LSTM without lag discipline (intentional leakage demo, reported as the leakage premium — this ablation is mandatory).\n228: 4. Training discipline: early stopping on walk-forward validation; seeds × 3, mean ± std reported.\n229: \n230: ### 5.5 Benchmarks (indicative)\n231: \n232: Regime AUC ≥ 0.75 walk-forward (classical baseline); nowcast error vs. a random-walk-with-drift benchmark; leakage ablation quantified.\n233: \n234: ---\n235: \n236: ## 6. Question 4 — China financial and trade networks\n237: \n238: Course mapping: Session 3 (KMeans, SQL, imbalance). Skills: graph construction, community detection, centrality, node embeddings, link prediction.\n239: \n240: ### 6.1 Data (public, verified)\n241: \n242: | Network | Source |\n243: |---|---|\n244: | A-share shareholding: top-10 (circulating) shareholders per stock per quarter | `akshare` `stock_gdfx` interfaces (46 endpoints, Eastmoney) |\n245: | Fund holdings: fund–stock quarterly portfolios | `ak.fund_portfolio_hold_em(symbol=..., date=...)` |\n246: | China trade partners: annual bilateral flows (HS, partner-level) | UN Comtrade public API, keyless: `comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS?reporterCode=156&period=...` |\n247: | Industry classification (ground truth) | `ak.stock_board_industry_*` / SW industry |\n248: \n249: Primary network (choose one, or both as A/B contrast): ownership network or trade network. Snapshot: ≥ 8 quarters (ownership) or ≥ 10 years (trade).\n250: \n251: ### 6.2 Common requirements\n252: \n253: - Construction rules stated as mathematics: e.g. correlation network $w_{ij} = \\sqrt{2(1-\\rho_{ij})}$ (price networks), bipartite holdings $B \\in \\{0,1\\}^{|F| \\times |S|}$ with weighted projection $W = B^\\top B$ (fund–stock), directed weighted trade graph $T_{ij}$ (value of exports $i \\to j$).\n254: - Graph statistics table per period: $|V|$, $|E|$, density, degree distribution (log–log fit), assortativity, connected components.\n255: - Verification duty: assert no self-loops, symmetric treatment where required, isolated nodes reported.\n256: \n257: ### 6.3 Option A — Network analytics (networkx)\n258: \n259: 1. Minimum spanning tree (Kruskal) of the metric distance network; evolution of tree diameter across periods.\n260: 2. Community detection: Louvain, modularity\n261:    $Q = \\frac{1}{2m}\\sum_{ij}\\Big[A_{ij} - \\frac{k_i k_j}{2m}\\Big]\\,\\delta(c_i, c_j)$;\n262:    compare communities with industry classification via ARI/NMI; resolution-sensitivity sweep.\n263: 3. Centrality: degree, betweenness, PageRank (iterative solution of $p = \\alpha P^\\top p + (1-\\alpha)\\mathbf{1}/n$, $\\alpha = 0.85$); ranked tables; interpretation (systemic firms / dominant trade partners).\n264: 4. Temporal analysis: community migration matrix between consecutive periods; identify structurally central nodes and structural breaks.\n265: \n266: ### 6.4 Option B — Node embeddings and link prediction (PyTorch)\n267: \n268: 1. node2vec (own implementation of the biased-walk skip-gram): objective $\\max_\\theta \\sum_v \\sum_{u \\in \\mathcal{N}(v)} \\log p_\\theta(u \\mid z_v)$; walk parameters $(p, q)$ swept.\n269: 2. Link prediction: score $s(u,v) = \\sigma(z_u^\\top W z_v)$; edges split 80/10/10 with equal negative sampling; metrics AUC, average precision; baselines: common-neighbors, Adamic–Adar, preferential attachment.\n270: 3. Task framing (choose per network): recover held-out holdings edges; predict industry membership from $z_v$ (linear probe); predict future trade-link formation $\\Delta T_{ij} > 0$.\n271: 4. Clustering the embedding space ($k$-means on $z_v$) vs. Louvain communities vs. industry labels (ARI/NMI matrix); embedding dimension swept $\\{8, 16, 32, 64\\}$.\n272: \n273: ### 6.5 Benchmarks (indicative)\n274: \n275: Link-prediction AUC ≥ 0.75 vs. ≥ 0.65 for the best heuristic baseline; ARI(embedding clusters, industry) reported against ARI(Louvain, industry).\n276: \n277: ---\n278: \n279: ## Appendix — Data source registry (verified 2026-10)\n280: \n281: | Source | Access | Status |\n282: |---|---|---|\n283: | akshare (MIT, 23k★, active) | `pip install akshare`, aliyun mirror | public |\n284: | SSE option chains (`option_current_day_sse`, daily stats) | akshare → sse.com.cn | public |\n285: | CFFEX index option contract lists & daily OHLCV | akshare → Sina Finance | public |\n286: | `macro_china_*` (170 series incl. Shibor/LPR/TSF/PMI) | akshare → Eastmoney/NBS mirrors | public |\n287: | `stock_gdfx` shareholder interfaces (46), `fund_portfolio_hold_em` | akshare → Eastmoney | public |\n288: | UN Comtrade preview API | keyless REST | public |\n289: | CNINFO disclosure API (annual-report PDFs, unauthenticated POST `hisAnnouncement/query` + `static.cninfo.com.cn`) | REST | public |\n290: | DuXiaoman FinCorpus (zh finance announcements/news, Apache-2.0) | `hf-mirror.com/datasets/Duxiaoman-DI/FinCorpus` | public |\n291: | CFSD labeled Chinese financial sentiment (Bian et al. 2019); Chinese financial sentiment dictionary | GitHub `seanxlwang/Bianetal2019CFSD`, `MengLingchao/Chinese_financial_sentiment_dictionary` | public |\n292: | FastboxData (SZSE L2 order book, CTP futures, Tushare daily) | read-only server, credentials via env | private, course-provided |\n293: | FX quotations SQLite (6 pairs, 2003–2020; interest rates CHF-only — caveat) | bundled on request | optional comparison dataset |\n294: \n295: General fallback rule: every external interface used by `fetch.py` must have a committed snapshot; grading runs offline."

              "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Reproducible data retrieval + offline snapshot for Question 2 (Monte Carlo pricing & hedging on Chinese futures).\n\nSources (all public, no credentials, via AKShare):\n  * CSI 300 stock-index futures main continuous contract (IF0, Sina finance via ``ak.futures_main_sina``)\n  * CSI 300 index daily history (000300, ``ak.index_zh_a_hist``)\n  * SHIBOR fixing history (``ak.macro_china_shibor_all``)\n\nUsage\n-----\n    uv run python data/fetch.py --help\n    uv run python data/fetch.py                 # verify committed snapshot (offline-safe)\n    uv run python data/fetch.py --verify-only   # only check SHA-256 of data/clean artifacts\n    uv run python data/fetch.py --refresh       # re-download from AKShare and rewrite snapshot+metadata\n\nThe committed snapshot in ``data/clean/`` is the authoritative offline fallback; a fresh clone\ncan run every downstream script without network access. ``--refresh`` re-fetches and rewrites\nboth ``data/clean/*.csv`` and ``data/metadata.json`` (source, retrieval date, schema, SHA-256).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport akshare as ak\nimport pandas as pd\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nCLEAN = ROOT / \"data\" / \"clean\"\nMETA = ROOT / \"data\" / \"metadata.json\"\n\nRETRIEVAL_DATE = date.today().isoformat()\nSTART_DATE = \"20170101\"  # futures main-contract history begins 2017-01-17\nEND_DATE = date.today().strftime(\"%Y%m%d\")\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Fetch + normalize\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef fetch_if_main() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    df = ak.futures_main_sina(symbol=\"IF0\")\n    df = df.rename(columns={\n        \"日期\": \"date\", \"开盘价\": \"open\", \"最高价\": \"high\", \"最低价\": \"low\",\n        \"收盘价\": \"close\", \"成交量\": \"volume\", \"持仓量\": \"open_interest\",\n    })\n    df = df[[\"date\", \"open\", \"high\", \"low\", \"close\", \"volume\", \"open_interest\"]].copy()\n    df[\"date\"] = pd.to_datetime(df[\"date\"]).dt.date.astype(str)\n    for c in [\"open\", \"high\", \"low\", \"close\", \"volume\", \"open_interest\"]:\n        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors=\"coerce\")\n    return df.sort_values(\"date\").reset_index(drop=True)\n\n\ndef fetch_csi300_index() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    df = ak.index_zh_a_hist(symbol=\"000300\", period=\"daily\", start_date=START_DATE, end_date=END_DATE)\n    df = df.rename(columns={\n        \"日期\": \"date\", \"开盘\": \"open\", \"收盘\": \"close\", \"最高\": \"high\", \"最低\": \"low\",\n        \"成交量\": \"volume\", \"成交额\": \"amount\", \"涨跌幅\": \"pct_change\",\n    })\n    df = df[[\"date\", \"open\", \"high\", \"low\", \"close\", \"volume\", \"amount\", \"pct_change\"]].copy()\n    df[\"date\"] = pd.to_datetime(df[\"date\"]).dt.date.astype(str)\n    for c in [\"open\", \"high\", \"low\", \"close\", \"volume\", \"amount\", \"pct_change\"]:\n        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors=\"coerce\")\n    return df.sort_values(\"date\").reset_index(drop=True)\n\n\ndef fetch_shibor() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    df = ak.macro_china_shibor_all()\n    keep = {\n        \"日期\": \"date\",\n        \"O/N-定价\": \"on\", \"1W-定价\": \"w1\", \"2W-定价\": \"w2\", \"1M-定价\": \"m1\",\n        \"3M-定价\": \"m3\", \"6M-定价\": \"m6\", \"9M-定价\": \"m9\", \"1Y-定价\": \"y1\",\n    }\n    df = df.rename(columns=keep)[list(keep.values())].copy()\n    df[\"date\"] = pd.to_datetime(df[\"date\"]).dt.date.astype(str)\n    df = df[df[\"date\"] >= \"2017-01-01\"]\n    for c in keep.values():\n        if c != \"date\":\n            df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors=\"coerce\")  # percent, e.g. 1.44 == 1.44%\n    return df.sort_values(\"date\").reset_index(drop=True)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Snapshot handling\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef sha256_of(path: Path) -> str:\n    h = hashlib.sha256()\n    with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b\"\"):\n            h.update(chunk)\n    return h.hexdigest()\n\n\ndef write_snapshot(frames: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict:\n    CLEAN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    artifacts = {}\n    for name, df in frames.items():\n        out = CLEAN / name\n        df.to_csv(out, index=False)\n        artifacts[name] = {\n            \"rows\": int(len(df)),\n            \"date_min\": str(df[\"date\"].min()),\n            \"date_max\": str(df[\"date\"].max()),\n            \"columns\": list(df.columns),\n            \"sha256\": sha256_of(out),\n        }\n    return artifacts\n\n\ndef load_metadata() -> dict:\n    if META.exists():\n        return json.loads(META.read_text())\n    return {}\n\n\ndef verify_snapshot() -> bool:\n    ok = True\n    meta = load_metadata()\n    artifacts = meta.get(\"artifacts\", {})\n    if not artifacts:\n        print(\"FAIL: data/metadata.json missing or has no artifacts; run with --refresh\")\n        return False\n    for name, info in artifacts.items():\n        path = CLEAN / name\n        if not path.exists():\n            print(f\"FAIL: missing {path}\")\n            ok = False\n            continue\n        digest = sha256_of(path)\n        status = \"OK\" if digest == info.get(\"sha256\") else \"FAIL\"\n        if status == \"FAIL\":\n            ok = False\n        print(f\"{status}  {name:24s} rows={info.get('rows')}  [{info.get('date_min')} .. {info.get('date_max')}]  sha256={digest[:12]}…\")\n    return ok\n\n\ndef build_metadata(artifacts: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"project\": \"Advanced Programming 2026 — Question 2: Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures\",\n        \"retrieval_date\": RETRIEVAL_DATE,\n        \"seed_note\": \"Data retrieval is deterministic given the AKShare endpoints; no randomness involved.\",\n        \"sources\": {\n            \"if_main.csv\": {\n                \"provider\": \"AKShare (ak.futures_main_sina) → Sina Finance\",\n                \"series\": \"CSI 300 stock-index futures, IF main continuous contract (IF0)\",\n                \"roll_convention\": \"AKShare 'main contract' continuous series; rolls on dominant open-interest/volume contract; artificial roll gaps possible in levels, mitigated by modelling log returns and disclosing the convention.\",\n                \"units\": \"index points (CNY per point × 300 per contract)\",\n            },\n            \"csi300_index.csv\": {\n                \"provider\": \"AKShare (ak.index_zh_a_hist) → Eastmoney\",\n                \"series\": \"CSI 300 index (000300) daily OHLCV\",\n                \"units\": \"index points\",\n            },\n            \"shibor.csv\": {\n                \"provider\": \"AKShare (ak.macro_china_shibor_all) → China Foreign Exchange Trade System / Eastmoney mirror\",\n                \"series\": \"Shanghai Interbank Offered Rate fixings, all tenors, daily\",\n                \"units\": \"percent per annum (e.g. 1.44 == 1.44%); converted to decimals in code\",\n            },\n        },\n        \"estimation_window\": {\n            \"full_history\": \"2017-01-17 .. present (as retrieved)\",\n            \"calibration_note\": \"Downstream scripts estimate μ, σ on trailing 5 calendar years of the retrieved history unless overridden; the window is stated in results/*/metrics.json.\",\n        },\n        \"missing_data_policy\": \"Rows with non-numeric or missing close are dropped; SHIBOR fixings are forward/back-filled only for curve interpolation, never for return estimation. Gaps (e.g. 2015-05 tabulated row) are reported by fetch.py --refresh.\",\n        \"transformations\": [\n            \"date normalized to ISO YYYY-MM-DD\",\n            \"prices cast to float64; volumes to float64\",\n            \"SHIBOR percent → decimal fraction only inside pricing code (r = y1 / 100)\",\n        ],\n        \"artifacts\": artifacts,\n    }\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--refresh\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"re-download from AKShare and rewrite snapshot + metadata.json\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--verify-only\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"only verify SHA-256 of committed snapshot (offline-safe)\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if args.verify_only:\n        return 0 if verify_snapshot() else 1\n\n    if args.refresh:\n        print(\"Downloading IF0 main continuous, CSI 300 index, SHIBOR …\")\n        frames = {\n            \"if_main.csv\": fetch_if_main(),\n            \"csi300_index.csv\": fetch_csi300_index(),\n            \"shibor.csv\": fetch_shibor(),\n        }\n        for name, df in frames.items():\n            n_na = int(df.isna().sum().sum())\n            print(f\"  {name:20s} rows={len(df)}  range=[{df['date'].min()} .. {df['date'].max()}]  NaN cells={n_na}\")\n        artifacts = write_snapshot(frames)\n        META.write_text(json.dumps(build_metadata(artifacts), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))\n        print(f\"Wrote {META}\")\n        return 0\n\n    # default: verify snapshot, then print coverage summary if possible\n    ok = verify_snapshot()\n    if ok:\n        try:\n            if_df = pd.read_csv(CLEAN / \"if_main.csv\")\n            print(f\"\\nCoverage OK: {len(if_df)} trading days, {if_df['date'].min()} .. {if_df['date'].max()} (>= 5 years required).\")\n        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - informational only\n            print(f\"(coverage summary unavailable: {exc})\")\n        return 0\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",

k, 0.0)\n\n\ndef payoff_asian(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    return np.maximum(paths[:, 1:].mean(axis=1) - k, 0.0)\n\n\ndef payoff_barrier(paths: np.ndarray, k: float, b: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    monitored = paths[:, 1:]\n    alive = monitored.max(axis=1) < b\n    return np.maximum(paths[:, -1] - k, 0.0) * alive\n\n\ndef payoff_digital(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    return (paths[:, -1] > k).astype(np.float64)\n\n\ndef geometric_average(paths: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    return np.exp(np.log(paths[:, 1:]).mean(axis=1))\n\n\ndef payoff_geometric_asian_call(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n    return np.maximum(geometric_average(paths) - k, 0.0)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Black-Scholes closed form + discrete-grid geometric Asian closed form\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef black_scholes_call(s0: float, k: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:\n    d1 = (math.log(s0 / k) + (r + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * t) / (sigma * math.sqrt(t))\n    d2 = d1 -           "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Aggregate results/approach*/**/metrics.json into comparison tables + results/comparison.html.\n\nUsage: uv run python code/compare.py\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport plotly.graph_objects as go\nfrom plotly.subplots import make_subplots\nfrom rich.console import Console\nfrom rich.table import Table\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nRESULTS = ROOT / \"results\"\nOUT_HTML = RESULTS / \"comparison.html\"\n\nconsole = Console()\n\n\ndef find_metrics() -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:\n    found = []\n    for path in sorted(RESULTS.glob(\"approach*/**/metrics.json\")):\n        try:\n            data = json.loads(path.read_text())\n        except Exception as exc:\n            console.print(f\"[red]Skipping unreadable {path}: {exc}[/red]\")\n            continue\n        label = str(path.parent.relative_to(RESULTS))\n        found.append((label, data))\n    return found\n\n\ndef flatten(d: dict, prefix: str = \"\") -> dict:\n    out = {}\n    for k, v in d.items():\n        key = f\"{prefix}{k}\"\n        if isinstance(v, dict):\n            out.update(flatten(v, key + \".\"))\n        else:\n            out[key] = v\n    return out\n\n\ndef print_metrics_table(title: str, label: str, flat: dict) -> None:\n    table = Table(title=f\"{title} — {label}\", show_lines=False)\n    table.add_column(\"metric\", style=\"cyan\", no_wrap=True)\n    table.add_column(\"value\", justify=\"right\")\n    for k, v in sorted(flat.items()):\n        if isinstance(v, float):\n            table.add_row(k, f\"{v:.6g}\")\n        else:\n            table.add_row(k, str(v)[:80])\n    console.print(table)\n\n\ndef cvar_rows(flat: dict) -> list[tuple[str, float, float, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Extract (method, mean_pnl, var_pnl, cvar95) rows if present (approach2 schema).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    # expect keys like metrics.neural_k0000.cvar95 or nested dicts already flattened\n    prefixes = sorted({k.rsplit(\".\", 1)[0] for k in flat if k.endswith(\".cvar95\")})\n    for p in prefixes:\n        cvar = flat.get(f\"{p}.cvar95\")\n        mean = flat.get(f\"{p}.mean_pnl\", flat.get(f\"{p}.expected_pnl\"))\n        var = flat.get(f\"{p}.var_pnl\", flat.get(f\"{p}.pnl_variance\"))\n        if cvar is not None:\n            rows.append((p, float(mean) if mean is not None else float(\"nan\"),\n                         float(var) if var is not None else float(\"nan\"), float(cvar)))\n    return rows\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    found = find_metrics()\n    if not found:\n        console.print(\"[yellow]No results/approach*/**/metrics.json found. Run the approach scripts first.[/yellow]\")\n        return\n\n    html_sections = []\n    for label, data in found:\n        params = flatten(data.get(\"params\", {}))\n        metrics = flatten(data.get(\"metrics\", {}))\n        print_metrics_table(\"Params\", label, params)\n        print_metrics_table(\"Metrics\", label, metrics)\n        console.print(f\"fit_seconds = {data.get('fit_seconds')}\\n\")\n        rows = cvar_rows(metrics)\n        if rows:\n            table = Table(title=f\"Ranked by CVaR(95%) ↑ — {label}\")\n            table.add_column(\"method\")\n            table.add_column(\"mean P&L\", justify=\"right\")\n            table.add_column(\"P&L variance\", justify=\"right\")\n            table.add_column(\"CVaR95\", justify=\"right\")\n            for name, mean, var, cvar in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[3]):\n                table.add_row(name, f\"{mean:.4f}\", f\"{var:.2f}\", f\"{cvar:.4f}\")\n            console.print(table)\n            fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=[r[0] for r in rows], y=[r[3] for r in rows],\n                                   name=\"CVaR95\"))\n            fig.update_layout(title=f\"CVaR(95%) by hedging method — {label}\",\n                              xaxis_title=\"method\", yaxis_title=\"CVaR of -V_T\")\n            html_sections.append(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=True))\n\n    OUT_HTML.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    body = \"<h1>Question 2 — Comparison of approach results</h1>\" + \"\\n\".join(html_sections) or \\\n           \"<p>No CVaR tables found; see approach metrics.json outputs.</p>\"\n    OUT_HTML.write_text(\n        \"<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset='utf-8'><title>Q2 comparison</title></head>\"\n        f\"<body>{body}</body></html>\"\n    )\n    console.print(f\"[green]Wrote {OUT_HTML}[/green]\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

              "content": "# Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures — Question 2 report\n\n**Advanced Programming 2026 · Question 2 (Option A + Option B) · Group report draft (agent-assisted; group to review and finalise)**\n\n> Status: DRAFT assembled from executed code and measured outputs. Every number quoted here is produced by the scripts in `code/` and stored in `results/approach*/if/metrics.json` (see §9 Reproducibility). Sections marked *[group to verify]* require group review before submission.\n\n## 1. Objective and scope\n\nWe price and hedge European-style claims written on the CSI 300 stock-index futures main continuous contract (IF0) using Monte Carlo methods under the risk-neutral measure, implement both a classical variance-reduction/Greeks toolchain (Option A) and a neural deep-hedging strategy trained by stochastic optimisation (Option B), and validate every estimator against closed-form benchmarks where available.\n\nDeliverables: this report, the repository (code + tests + data pipeline + comparison layer), `SESSION.md` (terminal-agent session export), and `AGENTS.md` (agent contract).\n\n## 2. Data and calibration\n\n### 2.1 Sources and provenance (see `data/metadata.json`)\n\n| Artefact | Source | Rows | Range |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `data/clean/if_main.csv` | AKShare `futures_main_sina` → Sina Finance; IF main continuous contract | 2374 | 2017-01-17 … 2026-11-02 |\n| `data/clean/csi300_index.csv` | AKShare `index_zh_a_hist` → Eastmoney; CSI 300 index (000300) | 2386 | 2017-01-03 … 2026-11-03 |\n| `data/clean/shibor.csv` | AKShare `macro_china_shibor_all` → CFETS/Eastmoney; SHIBOR all tenors | 2396 | 2017-03-17 … 2026-11-03 |\n\nAll three artefacts are committed (total < 0.5 MB) with SHA-256 hashes recorded in `data/metadata.json`; `uv run python data/fetch.py --verify-only` re-checks them offline and `--refresh` re-downloads. FastboxData credentials were not used; the public AKShare route was used instead, as permitted by the assignment (\"`ak.futures_main_sina`\").\n\n**Roll convention.** The IF0 series is AKShare's main-contract continuous series (dominant contract by volume/open interest). Roll gaps can induce artificial jumps in price *levels*; all estimation below uses **log returns**, which are roll-gap tolerant in practice but we flag that returns straddling rolls may embed small artefacts. No back-adjustment is applied; the series is used as displayed by the vendor.\n\n### 2.2 Estimation window and parameters\n\n* **Window:** trailing 5 calendar years, **2021-10-28 … 2026-11-02**, n = 1214 daily log returns of IF0 close. (Full history 2017–2026 was retrieved; the 5-year window matches the assignment's \"≥ 5 years\" requirement and avoids mixing pre-2021 regimes.)\n* **Physical drift (disclosure only):** μ̂ = mean(log-return) × 252 ≈ **−4.24 % p.a.** (not used in risk-neutral pricing).\n* **Volatility (used for pricing):** σ̂ = std(log-returns, ddof=1) × √252 ≈ **19.07 % p.a.** (full-sample 2017–2026: ≈ 20.08 %, reported for reference).\n* **Discount rate:** SHIBOR 1Y fixing 2026-11-03 = **1.4390 % p.a.** → r = 0.01439, flat for T = 1Y. No curve interpolation is required at this tenor; for other tenors we would linearly interpolate SHIBOR fixings in the rate (not in the discount factor).\n* **Spot:** S0 = **3974.8** (IF0 close 2026-11-02). **Strike:** K = S0 (spot-ATM). **Barrier:** B = 1.20 × S0 = 4769.76. **Maturity:** T = 1.0 y, **m = 252** monitors/year, dt = T/m.\n\n### 2.3 Model distinction (important)\n\nThe assignment prescribes simulation of the *futures price* with the GBM\n\nS(t+dt) = S(t) · exp[(r − σ²/2)·dt + σ·√dt·Z],  Z ~ N(0,1) i.i.d.\n\nWe implement exactly this for its Black–Scholes validation. Under standard risk-neutral theory a **futures price** is driftless (Black-76: dF = σ F dW̃). We deliberately do **not** silently conflate the two: the assignment-prescribed GBM-on-futures is used throughout, Black–Scholes-with-drift-r is its closed-form benchmark, and if a Black-76 cross-check is reported it is labelled separately as such. Physical-measure market risk (real-world drift, jump behaviour) is out of scope; our CVaR figures are **model-implied** under the risk-neutral simulator.\n\n## 3. Mathematical specification\n\n### 3.1 Exact GBM simulation (both engines)\n\nWith t_i = i·dt, log S_{t_i} = log S0 + Σ_{j<i} [(r − σ²/2)dt + σ√dt Z_j]; paths[:,0] = S0. NumPy engine: `np.random.default_rng(seed)`. PyTorch engine: `torch.Generator` (CPU), same recursion, independent seed (4242 in the cross-engine check; 42 elsewhere). Minimum 252 steps/year as prescribed. Antithetic sampling uses pairs (Z, −Z) with an even number of paths.\n\n### 3.2 Payoffs (monitored on t_1..t_m; **S_0 is NOT monitored**)\n\n1. Arithmetic Asian call: A = max(mean(S_{t_1..m}) − K, 0)\n2. Up-and-out call, discrete monitoring: B(S) = max(S_T − K, 0) · 1{max(S_{t_1..m}) < B}\n3. Digital call: D = 1{S_T > K}\n4. European vanilla call (validation benchmark): E = max(S_T − K, 0)\n\n### 3.3 Black–Scholes benchmark and validation duty\n\nEuropean call: C_BS = S0·N(d1) − K e^{−rT} N(d2), d1,2 = [ln(S0/K) ± (r ± σ²/2)T]/(σ√T). Validation: z = (MC − C_BS)/SE_MC, PASS iff |z| ≤ 3. Reported in §4.1.\n\n### 3.4 Geometric Asian control variate (exact discrete moments)\n\nFor the same discrete grid, G = (Π S_{t_i})^{1/m} is lognormal with\n\nμ_G = ln S0 + (r − σ²/2)·T·(m+1)/(2m),   var_G = σ²T²·(m+1)(2m+1)/(6m²),\n\nE[G] = e^{μ_G + var_G/2}, and the geometric-Asian call price has the Black–Scholes-type closed form (d1 = (μ_G − ln K + var_G)/√var_G). The control-variate estimator for the arithmetic Asian call uses per-path geometric payoffs as the control with the closed-form geometric-Asian call as the reference expectation; β̂ = Ĉov(A,G)/V̂ar(G) estimated in-sample (asymptotically unbiased at N = 2^17).\n\n### 3.5 Greeks\n\n* **Pathwise (valid only for a.s. differentiable payoffs):**\n  delta_vanilla = e^{−rT} E[1{S_T>K}·S_T/S0]; delta_asian = e^{−rT} E[1{A>K}·(1/m Σ S_i)/S0];\n  vega_asian = e^{−rT} E[1{A>K}·(1/m Σ S_i·(√t_i Z_i − σ t_i))].\n* **Central finite differences with common random numbers:** spot bump h ∈ {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}·S0; vega uses absolute vol bumps ε ∈ {0.1, 0.01, 0.001} (i.e. h/S0-scaled, documented). Common random numbers make the FD estimator's variance finite and its bias O(h²).\n* **Digital and barrier payoffs are discontinuous** ⇒ naive pathwise differentiation yields 0 a.s. (the indicator's derivative is a Dirac mass) and is *not* reported as an estimator; FD is reported instead, and the bias/variance tradeoff across h is analysed.\n* BS analytic delta (N(d1)) and vega (S0·√T·N′(d1)) reported for the vanilla as ground truth.\n\n### 3.6 Convergence and verification protocol\n\nRMSE(N) over N ∈ {2^8,…,2^17}, R = 20 independent replications per N; log10–log10 fit of RMSE vs N; fitted slope compared against the theoretical −1/2 with its OLS standard error (assumption: independent replications; reported, not assumed). Antithetic halves the variance for positively-correlated monotone payoffs; control variate removes the geometric component of variance exactly.\n\n### 3.7 Option B — deep hedging specification\n\n* Payoff: European vanilla call (cleanest analytic BS-delta benchmark).\n* Policy: Δ_i = f_θ(S_i/S0, t_i/T); MLP ≤ 3 hidden layers (64-64-64, ReLU, linear output). Decisions use only F_{t_i}.\n* Accounting (assignment formula, exact conventions): hedging grid t_i = i·dt, i = 0..m−1; Δ_i set at t_i;\n  V_T = Σ_i e^{r(T−t_i)} Δ_i (S_{i+1} − S_i) − κ Σ_i |Δ_i − Δ_{i−1}|·S_{t_i} − H(S_T),  Δ_{−1} := 0\n  (initial position charged; costs at decision-time spot; **no extra closeout term** — the final hedging P&L leg realises the last move).\n* Premium: **excluded** exactly as the assignment writes; adding the constant e^{rT}·C_BS would shift mean P&L (and CVaR) identically across all policies and leave the variance and all policy rankings unchanged.\n* Objective: L = −V_T; minimise empirical CVaR_0.95(L) in the Rockafellar–Uryasev form min_{θ,η} η + (1/(1−α))·mean(relu(L − η)), α = 0.95, η learnable. Out-of-sample CVaR evaluated directly (mean of worst 5%) independently of the training loss.\n* Training: N_train = 2^17 = 131072 simulated paths (seed 42); validation 2^15 paths (seed 123) with early stopping (patience 12); test 2^15 paths (seed 2026) never touched during training. Minibatches, Adam.\n* Benchmarks: BS delta Δ = N(d1(t,S)) with recomputed τ = T−t, at rebalancing frequencies {1, 5, 21} days and κ ∈ {0, 0.001, 0.005} (0/10/50 bp) — 9 combinations — plus the neural policy at the same three κ levels (every-step rebalancing). Metrics on test paths: E[V_T], Var(V_T), CVaR_0.95(−V_T), turnover Σ|ΔΔ|, mean cost per path.\n* The same accounting applies to neural and baseline policies (identical cost model, premium exclusion, discounting).\n\n## 4. Results\n\n*[TO BE FILLED FROM results/approach1/if/metrics.json and results/approach2/if/metrics.json after the experiment runs; figures referenced from results/.]*\n\n## 5. Discussion and limitations\n\n* GBM-with-drift is the assignment's model; real futures exhibit mean-reversion/jumps and the physical drift is negative in the sample — none of this enters the risk-neutral price.\n* Continuous main contract roll gaps; log-return mitigation; no back-adjustment.\n* Discrete monitoring (252/y) of barrier/average; continuous monitoring would change values (barrier especially; discrete is the assignment's spec).\n* Risk-neutral CVaR ≠ real-world market risk; deep-hedge advantage (if any) is relative to the simulator's measure and the vanilla call payoff.\n* SHIBOR 1Y flat for T=1Y; no dividend/convenience-yield modelling; futures basis not modelled (assignment prescribes GBM on the futures level).\n* Asian/barrier Greeks by FD have O(h²) bias; pathwise invalid there.\n* Neural results hold only out-of-sample (test seed 2026); in-sample training fit is not evidence of hedging skill.\n\n## 6. Statement of work (agents vs group)\n\n* **ChatGPT/OpenAI lead agent (this session):** specification & conventions, data pipeline (`data/fetch.py`), provenance/checksums, shared mathematics (`code/mc_common.py`), tests, `compare.py`, README, report drafting, Git integration, verification of all claims against measured outputs.\n* **DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-pro, via OpenCode subagents):** implementation of `code/approach1_pricing.py` and `code/approach2_hedging.py` (engines, variance reduction, Greeks, convergence, profiling, MLP, CVaR training, benchmark sweeps), and execution of the experiments.\n* **Kimi (independent review):** cross-file audit of math/code/results; findings recorded in §7; fixes applied by the lead/DeepSeek and re-verified.\n* **The group:** mathematical decisions (model choice, payoff conventions, monitoring, benchmark design), verification of results, final wording and submission of this report; the agent-produced draft is not the group's sign-off.\n\n## 7. Independent audit (Kimi) and repairs\n\n*[TO BE FILLED after the Kimi review; findings, severity, disposition, and re-verification results.]*\n\n## 8. Reproducibility\n\nFresh clone: `uv sync --frozen` (UV_CACHE_DIR=.cache/uv), then the commands in README.md (≤10 lines). Offline: snapshot committed; `--verify-only` checks SHA-256. Seeds: 42 (train/main), 123 (val), 2026 (test), 4242 (torch cross-check). Nondeterminism: torch CPU ops may be multithreaded; results are reproducible up to BLAS threading noise; no GPU used. `results/` is gitignored and regenerable; `data/clean/` is committed.\n\n## 9. Figure index\n\n* `results/approach1/if/convergence.html` — RMSE vs N, log–log, with fitted slopes (target −1/2)\n* `results/approach1/if/var_reduction.html` — variance-reduction factors (antithetic, control variate)\n* `results/approach1/if/greeks.html` — FD bias/variance vs h (if produced)\n* `results/approach1/if/line_profile.txt` — hot-loop profile\n* `results/approach2/if/training_curve.html` — train/val CVaR vs epoch\n* `results/approach2/if/pnl_distribution.html` — test P&L distributions\n* `results/approach2/if/benchmark_bars.html` — CVaR95 across hedging methods\n* `results/comparison.html` — aggregated comparison (code/compare.py)\n",

delta_prev).abs()\n    cost = kappa * (trade * s_spot).sum(dim=1)\n    turnover = trade.sum(dim=1)\n\n    payoff = torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - k, min=0.0)  # H(S_T) = max(S_T - K, 0)\n    V = hedge_gain - cost - payoff\n    return V, turnover, cost\n\n\ndef empirical_cvar(loss: torch.Tensor, alpha: float = ALPHA) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Empirical CVaR_alpha of a loss vector (independent of the R-U training loss).\n\n    Sort descending, average the worst (1-alpha) fraction (the upper tail of L).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = loss.numel()\n    k = max(1, int(round((1 - alpha) * n)))\n    sorted_desc, _ = torch.sort(loss, descending=True)\n    return float(sorted_desc[:k].mean().item())\n\n\ndef policy_loss(model: HedgeMLP, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, k: float, r: float,\n                dt: float, m: int, kappa: float) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"L = -V_T for the neural policy on paths S (loss, larger is worse).\"\"\"\n    delta = neural_delta(model, S, s0, m)\n    V, _, _ = hedge_pnl(S, delta, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n    return -V\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Black-Scholes delta benchmark\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef bs_delta(S_spot: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float, sigma: float,\n             tau: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"N(d1) with d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + sigma^2/2)*tau) / (sigma*sqrt(tau)).\"\"\"\n    d1 = (torch.log(S_spot / k) + (r + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * tau) / (sigma * torch.sqrt(tau))\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + torch.erf(d1 / math.sqrt(2.0)))\n\n\ndef bs_delta_hedge(S: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float,\n                   m: int, freq: int) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"BS-delta positions (n_paths, m), rebalanced every `freq` steps and held in between.\n\n    Trades occur ONLY at rebalance dates i in {0, freq, 2*freq, ...}; between those dates the\n    position is held constant (no trade, no cost).  Cost is still charged on |DeltaDelta| at the\n    rebalance dates via the shared hedge_pnl (which uses Delta_{i-1}).\n    \"\"\"\n    dt = t / m\n    i = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=torch.long)\n    tau = (m - i).to(S.dtype) * dt            # remaining time at each potential rebalance point\n    s_spot = S[:, :-1]\n    target = bs_delta(s_spot, k, r, sigma, tau)   # full target delta at every step (cheap)\n    rebalance_col = (i // freq) * freq        # last rebalance index <= i (int64)\n    return target[:, rebalance_col]           # (n, m) held-constant positions\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Training (Rockafellar-Uryasev CVaR)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef train_model(model: HedgeMLP, eta: nn.Parameter, S_train: torch.Tensor, S_val: torch.Tensor,\n                s0: float, k: float, r: float, dt: float, m: int, kappa: float, alpha: float,\n                lr: float, eta_lr: float, epochs: int, batch_size: int, patience: int,\n                min_delta: float, shuffle_seed: int, console: Console):\n    n = S_train.shape[0]\n    # Warm-start eta at the empirical CVaR_alpha of the UNHEDGED loss (L = payoff when Delta=0)\n    # so the Rockafellar-Uryasev objective targets the tail from the first update.  Adam\n    # normalises its update magnitude, so a cold eta=0 would climb ~lr per batch (~0.03/epoch)\n    # and never reach the O(10^3) quantile within the epoch budget; a separate (higher) eta lr\n    # lets eta track the slowly-moving quantile thereafter.\n    n_train_eval = min(n, 32768)\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        payoff0 = torch.clamp(S_train[:n_train_eval, -1] - k, min=0.0)\n        eta.data.fill_(empirical_cvar(payoff0, alpha))\n    console.print(f\"[dim]eta warm-start = {float(eta.item()):.1f} (empirical CVaR of unhedged loss)[/]\")\n\n    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([\n        {\"params\": model.parameters(), \"lr\": lr},\n        {\"params\": [eta], \"lr\": eta_lr},\n    ], lr=lr)\n    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(shuffle_seed)\n    n_batches = (n + batch_size - 1) // batch_size\n    S_train_eval = S_train[:n_train_eval]\n\n    history = {\"epoch\": [], \"train_loss\": [], \"train_cvar\": [], \"val_cvar\": []}\n    best_val_cvar = float(\"inf\")\n    best_state, best_eta = None, None\n    epochs_no_improve = 0\n    rho = 1.0 / (1.0 - alpha)             # = 20\n\n    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):\n        model.train()\n        perm = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)\n        total_loss = 0.0\n        for b in range(n_batches):\n            idx = perm[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]\n            S_batch = S_train[idx]\n            L = policy_loss(model, S_batch, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            loss = eta + rho * torch.relu(L - eta).mean()\n            optimizer.zero_grad()\n            loss.backward()\n            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(list(model.parameters()) + [eta], 10.0)\n            optimizer.step()\n            total_loss += float(loss.item()) * int(idx.numel())\n\n        avg_train_loss = total_loss / n\n        model.eval()\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            L_train = policy_loss(model, S_train_eval, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            train_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_train, alpha)\n            L_val = policy_loss(model, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            val_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_val, alpha)\n\n        history[\"epoch\"].append(epoch)\n        history[\"train_loss\"].append(avg_train_loss)\n        history[\"train_cvar\"].append(train_cvar)\n        history[\"val_cvar\"].append(val_cvar)\n\n        if epoch == 1 or epoch % 5 == 0:\n            console.print(\n                f\"[cyan]epoch {epoch:3d}[/]  train_loss={avg_train_loss:8.4f}  \"\n                f\"train_cvar={train_cvar:9.4f}  val_cvar={val_cvar:9.4f}  \"\n                f\"eta={float(eta.item()):8.1f}\")\n\n        if val_cvar < best_val_cvar - min_delta:\n            best_val_cvar = val_cvar\n            epochs_no_improve = 0\n            best_state = {kk: vv.detach().clone() for kk, vv in model.state_dict().items()}\n            best_eta = eta.detach().clone()\n        else:\n            epochs_no_improve += 1\n            if epochs_no_improve >= patience:\n                console.print(f\"[yellow]early stopping at epoch {epoch} \"\n                              f\"(no improvement > {min_delta} for {patience} epochs)[/]\")\n                break\n\n    if best_state is not None:\n        model.load_state_dict(best_state)\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            eta.copy_(best_eta)\n\n    return history, best_val_cvar\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Evaluation helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef evaluate_policy(delta_fn, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, k: float, r: float,\n                    dt: float, m: int, kappa: float, alpha: float):\n"

                "type": "text",
                "text": "    return x.reshape(-1, 2)\n\n\ndef neural_delta(model: HedgeMLP, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, m: int) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Return delta (n_paths, m): Delta_i = f_theta(S_{t_i}/S_0, t_i/T).\"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    x = policy_inputs(S, s0, m)\n    return model(x).reshape(n, m)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Hedging P&L (assignment formula, shared by neural and BS policies)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef hedge_pnl(S: torch.Tensor, delta: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float,\n              dt: float, m: int, kappa: float):\n    \"\"\"Terminal hedging P&L per the assignment formula.\n\n    Args:\n        S:      (n_paths, m+1) asset path, S[:, 0] == S_0.\n        delta:  (n_paths, m) position Delta_i decided at t_i.\n    Returns:\n        V:          (n_paths,) terminal P&L (premium excluded).\n        turnover:   (n_paths,) sum_i |Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}|.\n        cost:       (n_paths,) kappa * sum_i |Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}| * S_{t_i}.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    dS = S[:, 1:] - S[:, :-1]                    # (n, m)  S_{i+1} - S_i\n    i = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype)\n    discount = torch.exp(r * (m - i) * dt)       # (m,)  exp(r*(T - t_i))\n    hedge_gain = (delta * dS * discount).sum(dim=1)\n\n"
              }

This module only implements the Option-B deep-hedging\npipeline (single self-contained script, argparse, linear load -> simulate -> fit -> evaluate ->\nwrite outputs), per the assignment §4.4 and the AGENTS.md Option-B contract.\n\nAccounting conventions (documented here AND in metrics.json, and echoed in the terminal):\n  * Hedging grid t_i = i*dt, i = 0..m-1, m = 252 steps, dt = T/m = 1/252.                 "type": "text",
                "text": "# Training (Rockafellar-Uryasev CVaR)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef train_model(model: HedgeMLP, eta: nn.Parameter, S_train: torch.Tensor, S_val: torch.Tensor,\n                s0: float, k: float, r: float, dt: float, m: int, kappa: float, alpha: float,\n                lr: float, epochs: int, batch_size: int, patience: int,\n                min_delta: float, shuffle_seed: int, console: Console):\n    \"\"\"Minimise CVaR_alpha(L), L = -V_T, via the Rockafellar-Uryasev form solved by\n    coordinate descent.\n\n    The R-U objective  min_{theta, eta}  eta + (1/(1-alpha))*E[relu(L_theta - eta)] is\n    jointly minimised by (i) an EXACT eta-step and (ii) a gradient theta-step:\n\n      * For fixed theta, the objective is convex in eta and its minimiser is the empirical\n        alpha-quantile (VaR_alpha) of L_theta:  P(L > eta*) = 1 - alpha.  We recompute\n        eta = quantile_alpha(L_theta) on a fixed training subset at the START of every epoch.\n      * For fixed eta, we take Adam gradient steps on theta through\n        eta + rho * mean(relu(L_theta - eta)); only the paths with L > eta (the upper tail)\n        contribute gradient.\n\n    A purely gradient-based update of eta is NOT used because Adam normalises the update\n    magnitude to ~lr per step, so eta would track the VaR far too slowly (the VaR drops by\n    O(10^3) points as the policy learns to hedge); the exact quantile step sidesteps this.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S_train.shape[0]\n    n_train_eval = min(n, 16384)          # fixed subset for quantile/VaR and train-CVaR reporting\n    S_train_eval = S_train[:n_train_eval]\n    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)\n    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(shuffle_seed)\n    n_batches = (n + batch_size - 1) // batch_size\n    rho = 1.0 / (1.0 - alpha)\n\n    # Initial eta = VaR_alpha of the UNHEDGED loss (L = payoff when Delta ~ 0).  Each epoch\n    # reuses the end-of-epoch train loss for BOTH the train-CVaR report and the next epoch's\n    # eta, so the train-eval subset is forwarded exactly once per epoch.\n    model.eval()\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        L_train = policy_loss(model, S_train_eval, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n    eta_q = float(torch.quantile(L_train, alpha).item())\n\n    history = {\"epoch\": [], \"train_loss\": [], \"train_cvar\": [], \"val_cvar\": [], \"eta\": []}\n    best_val_cvar = float(\"inf\")\n    best_state, best_eta = None, None\n    epochs_no_improve = 0\n\n    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):\n        eta_used = eta_q\n        eta.data.fill_(eta_used)           # exact R-U minimiser in eta (VaR_alpha)\n\n        model.train()\n        perm = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)\n        total_loss = 0.0\n        for b in range(n_batches):\n            idx = perm[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]\n            L = policy_loss(model, S_train[idx], s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            loss = eta_used + rho * torch.relu(L - eta_used).mean()\n            optimizer.zero_grad()\n            loss.backward()\n            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 10.0)\n            optimizer.step()\n            total_loss += float(loss.item()) * int(idx.numel())\n\n        avg_train_loss = total_loss / n\n        model.eval()\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            L_train = policy_loss(model, S_train_eval, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            train_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_train, alpha)\n            eta_q = float(torch.quantile(L_train, alpha).item())   # eta for next epoch\n            L_val = policy_loss(model, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            val_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_val, alpha)\n\n        history[\"epoch\"].append(epoch)\n        history[\"train_loss\"].append(avg_train_loss)\n        history[\"train_cvar\"].append(train_cvar)\n        history[\"val_cvar\"].append(val_cvar)\n        history[\"eta\"].append(eta_used)\n\n        if epoch == 1 or epoch % 5 == 0:\n            console.print(\n                f\"[cyan]epoch {epoch:3d}[/]  train_loss={avg_train_loss:8.4f}  \"\n                f\"train_cvar={train_cvar:9.4f}  val_cvar={val_cvar:9.4f}  \"\n                f\"eta={eta_used:8.1f}\")\n\n        if val_cvar < best_val_cvar - min_delta:\n            best_val_cvar = val_cvar\n            epochs_no_improve = 0\n            best_state = {kk: vv.detach().clone() for kk, vv in model.state_dict().items()}\n            best_eta = eta.detach().clone()\n        else:\n            epochs_no_improve += 1\n            if epochs_no_improve >= patience:\n                console.print(f\"[yellow]early stopping at epoch {epoch} \"\n"

<= 3 hidden layers, causal)\")\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 3. Train\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    console.print(f\"[bold]Training[/] N_train={args.n_train} N_val={args.n_val} lr={args.lr} \"\n                  f\"batch={args.batch_size} max_epochs={args.epochs} kappa={args.train_kappa}\")\n    t0 = time.perf_counter()\n    history, best_val_cvar = train_model(\n        model, eta, S_train, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, args.train_kappa, ALPHA,\n        args.lr, args.epochs, args.batch_size, args.patience, args.min_delta,\n        args.seed, console)\n    fit_seconds = time.perf_counter() - t0\n    n_epochs_run = len(history[\"epoch\"])\n    console.print(f\"[bold]Training done[/] {n_epochs_run} epochs in {fit_seconds:.1f}s \"\n                  f\"best_val_cvar={best_val_cvar:.4f}\")\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 4.               "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Paired bootstrap of out-of-sample CVaR differences: Neural vs BS-delta hedging.\n\nReads the per-path TEST losses dumped by approach2_hedging.py\n(`results/approach2/if/test_losses.npz`, losses L = -V_T on the SAME 2^15 test paths,\nseed 2026) and computes, for each transaction cost level κ ∈ {0, 10, 50} bp:\n\n    ΔCVaR = CVaR_0.95(L_neural) − CVaR_0.95(L_bs_fX_κ)\n\nwhere X ∈ {1, 5, 21} days (BS-1d is the primary comparator). The bootstrap resamples\npaths with replacement (B replicates, seed 42) and recomputes both CVaRs and their\ndifference on each resample (\"paired\" — both policies are always evaluated on the same\nresampled paths). Reported: point estimate, bootstrap mean, 2.5/97.5 percentiles,\nfraction of resamples with ΔCVaR < 0 (neural better), and the input SEs.\n\nUsage:  uv run python code/bootstrap_cvar.py [--boot 10000] [--seed 42] [--alpha 0.95]\nOutput: results/approach2/if/bootstrap_cvar.json + rich tables.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom rich.console import Console\nfrom rich.table import Table\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nLOSSES = ROOT / \"results\" / \"approach2\" / \"if\" / \"test_losses.npz\"\nOUT = ROOT / \"results\" / \"approach2\" / \"if\" / \"bootstrap_cvar.json\"\n\n\ndef cvar(loss: np.ndarray, alpha: float) -> float:\n    n = loss.shape[0]\n    k = max(1, int(round((1.0 - alpha) * n)))\n    return float(np.sort(loss)[::-1][:k].mean())\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,\n                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--boot\", type=int, default=10000, help=\"bootstrap resamples (default 10000)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=42)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--alpha\", type=float, default=0.95)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if not LOSSES.exists():\n        print(f\"FAIL: {LOSSES} not found; run code/approach2_hedging.py first.\")\n        return 1\n\n    data = np.load(LOSSES)\n    losses = {k: data[k] for k in data.files}\n    n = len(losses[\"neural_0bp\"])\n    console = Console()\n    console.print(f\"[bold]Paired bootstrap[/] n_test={n}  B={args.boot}  seed={args.seed}  alpha={args.alpha}\")\n\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)\n    results = {}\n    for kappa in [\"0bp\", \"10bp\", \"50bp\"]:\n        neural = losses[f\"neural_{kappa}\"]\n        for freq in [1, 5, 21]:\n            bs = losses[f\"bs_f{freq}_{kappa}\"]\n            point = cvar(neural, args.alpha) - cvar(bs, args.alpha)\n            boots = np.empty(args.boot)\n            for b in range(args.boot):\n                idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)\n                boots[b] = cvar(neural[idx], args.alpha) - cvar(bs[idx], args.alpha)\n            lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])\n            frac_neg = float((boots < 0.0).mean())\n            key = f\"neural_vs_bs_f{freq}_{kappa}\"\n            results[key] = {\n                \"cvar_neural\": cvar(neural, args.alpha),\n                \"cvar_bs\": cvar(bs, args.alpha),\n                \"delta_cvar\": point,\n                \"boot_mean\": float(boots.mean()),\n                \"ci95_low\": float(lo),\n                \"ci95_high\": float(hi),\n                \"frac_boot_neural_better\": frac_neg,\n                \"corr_paths\": float(np.corrcoef(neural, bs)[0, 1]),\n            }\n            table = Table(title=f\"ΔCVaR95 = neural − BS-{freq}d   (κ = {kappa})\")\n            table.add_column(\"metric\"); table.add_column(\"value\", justify=\"right\")\n            table.add_row(\"CVaR neural\", f\"{results[key]['cvar_neural']:.3f}\")\n            table.add_row(\"CVaR BS\", f\"{results[key]['cvar_bs']:.3f}\")\n            table.add_row(\"ΔCVaR (point)\", f\"{point:+.3f}\")\n            table.add_row(\"bootstrap mean ± sd\", f\"{boots.mean():+.3f} ± {boots.std(ddof=1):.3f}\")\n            table.add_row(\"95% percentile CI\", f\"[{lo:+.3f}, {hi:+.3f}]\")\n            table.add_row(\"P(neural better) bootstrap\", f\"{frac_neg:.3f}\")\n            table.add_row(\"corr(L_neural, L_bs) across paths\", f\"{results[key]['corr_paths']:.3f}\")\n            console.print(table)\n\n    payload = {\"params\": {\"boot\": args.boot, \"seed\": args.seed, \"alpha\": args.alpha,\n                          \"n_test\": n, \"losses_file\": str(LOSSES.relative_to(ROOT))},\n               \"metrics\": results,\n               \"fit_seconds\": None,\n               \"history\": {}}\n    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))\n    # note: fit_seconds is deliberately null — this is a post-processing bootstrap, not a fit.\n    console.print(f\"[green]Wrote {OUT}[/green]\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n",
              "path": "code/bootstrap_cvar.py"
            },

              "newString": "def test_geo_moments_positive_variance():\n    mu_g, var_g = mc.geometric_asian_moments(P.s0, P.r, P.sigma, P.t, mc.M)\n    assert var_g > 0\n    assert math.isfinite(mu_g)\n\n\ndef test_geo_variance_exact_discrete_sum():\n    \"\"\"Regression test: var_G must equal sigma^2 * (T/m)/m^2 * sum_{i,j} min(i,j),\n    with sum_{i,j} min(i,j) = m(m+1)(2m+1)/6 — for T != 1 (catches the T^2 bug).\"\"\"\n    for t_years in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 7.3):\n        for m in (1, 2, 12, 252):\n            s0, r, sigma = 100.0, 0.03, 0.25\n            _, var_g = mc.geometric_asian_moments(s0, r, sigma, t_years, m)\n            dt = t_years / m\n            min_sum = sum(min(i, j) for i in range(1, m + 1) for j in range(1, m + 1))\n            assert min_sum == pytest.approx(m * (m + 1) * (2 * m + 1) / 6)\n            expected = sigma * sigma * dt / (m * m) * min_sum\n            assert var_g == pytest.approx(expected, rel=1e-12)\n            # also equals closed form sigma^2 * T * (m+1)(2m+1) / (6 m^2)\n            assert var_g == pytest.approx(sigma * sigma * t_years * (m + 1) * (2 * m + 1) / (6 * m * m), rel=1e-12)",

Let me write a dedicated vectorized function that does the full pipeline in explicit steps:\n\n```python\ndef asian_vectorized(z, s0, r, sigma, t, m, k):\n    dt = t / m\n    drift = (r - 0.5*sigma*sigma) * dt\n    diffusion = sigma * math.sqrt(dt) * z\n    log_inc = drift + diffusion\n    log_paths = np.concatenate([np.zeros((z.shape[0],1)), np.cumsum(log_inc, axis=1)], axis=1)\n    paths = s0 * np.exp(log_paths)\n    avg = paths[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)\n    payoff = np.maximum(avg - k, 0.0)\n    return payoff.mean()\n```\n\nThis way line_profiler shows each numpy op.
