k)             # undiscounted geometric call payoff\n    mu_g_undisc = mc.geometric_asian_call_price(s0, k, r, sigma, t, m) / d\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    cov = np.cov(A, G, ddof=1)[0, 1]\n    var_g = np.var(G, ddof=1)\n    beta = float(cov / var_g)\n    theta_cv = A.mean() - beta * (G.mean() - mu_g_undisc)\n    price = float(d * theta_cv)\n    var_a = float(np.var(A, ddof=1))\n    var_cv_undisc = (var_a - beta * beta * var_g) / n\n    var_cv = d * d * var_cv_undisc\n    var_naive = d * d * var_a / n\n    vr = var_a / max(var_a - beta * beta * var_g, 1e-300)\n    return beta, price, math.sqrt(var_cv), var_cv, var_naive, float(vr)\n\n\ndef antithetic_price(paths: np.ndarray, k: float, r: float, t: float):\n    \"\"\"Antithetic estimate via paired (Z, -Z) rows; SE from pair-averaged payoffs.\"\"\"\n    d = math.exp(-r * t)\n    payoff = mc.payoff_asian(paths, k)  # undiscounted\n    n = payoff.shape[0]\n    pair_mean = payoff.reshape(n // 2, 2).mean(axis=1)\n    est = float(d * pair_mean.mean())\n    var_est = float(d * d * np.var(pair_mean, ddof=1) / (n // 2))\n    return est, math.sqrt(var_est), var_est\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Pathwise Greeks\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef brownian_increments(z: np.ndarray, t: float, m: int):\n    \"\"\"Return (W, times): W[i] = Brownian value at t_i, times = (t_1..t_m).\"\"\"\n    dt = t / m\n    W = math.sqrt(dt) * np.cumsum(z, axis=1)\n    times = dt * np.arange(1, m + 1)\n    return W, times\n\n\ndef pathwise_greeks(paths: np.ndarray, z: np.ndarray, p, name: str):\n    \"\"\"Pathwise delta & vega. Valid only for a.s. differentiable payoffs (vanilla, Asian).\"\"\"\n    d = math.exp(-p.r * p.t)\n    W, times = brownian_increments(z, p.t, p.m)\n    n = paths.shape[0]\n    if name == \"vanilla\":\n        s_t = paths[:, -1]\n        ind = (s_t > p.k).astype(np.float64)\n        delta_terms = d * ind * s_t / p.s0\n        vega_terms = d * ind * s_t * (W[:, -1] - p.sigma * p.t)\n    elif name == \"asian\":\n        s_mon = paths[:, 1:]                       # (n, m)\n        avg = s_mon.mean(axis=1)\n        ind = (avg > p.k).astype(np.float64)\n        delta_deriv = s_mon.mean(axis=1) / p.s0\n        vega_deriv = (s_mon * (W - p.sigma * times[None, :])).mean(axis=1)\n        delta_terms = d * ind * delta_deriv\n        vega_terms = d * ind * vega_deriv\n    else:\n        raise ValueError(f\"pathwise not valid for {name}\")\n    delta = float(delta_terms.mean())\n    vega = float(vega_terms.mean())\n    delta_se = float(delta_terms.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n    vega_se = float(vega_terms.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n    return delta, delta_se, vega, vega_se\n\n\ndef fd_greek(name: str, z: np.ndarray, p, bump: float, which: str):\n    \"\"\"Central finite difference with common random numbers (same z for +/- bump).\n    Returns (estimate, se) using the per-path difference so the SE reflects the CRN pairing.\"\"\"\n    d = math.exp(-p.r * p.t)\n    if which == \"delta\":\n        paths_up = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0 + bump, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z)\n        paths_dn = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0 - bump, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z)\n    else:  # vega\n        paths_up = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma + bump, p.t, p.m, z)\n        paths_dn = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma - bump, p.t, p.m, z)\n    pu = compute_payoff(name, paths_up, p.k, p.barrier)\n    pd = compute_payoff(name, paths_dn, p.k, p.barrier)\n    g_i = d * (pu - pd) / (2.0 * bump)\n    n = g_i.shape[0]\n    est = float(g_i.mean())\n    se = float(g_i.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n    return est, se\n\n\ndef bs_greeks(p):\n    d1 = (math.log(p.s0 / p.k) + (p.r + 0.5 * p.sigma ** 2) * p.t) / (p.sigma * math.sqrt(p.t))\n    delta = norm.cdf(d1)\n    vega = p.s0 * math.sqrt(p.t) * norm.pdf(d1)  # per unit sigma\n    return float(delta), float(vega)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# High-precision Asian reference (chunked control variate)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef asian_reference(p, n_ref: int = 2 ** 21, chunk: int = 2 ** 18, seed: int = 42):\n    d = math.exp(-p.r * p.t)\n    mu_g = mc.geometric_asian_call_price(p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m) / d\n    # pilot beta from a single chunk\n    z0 = mc.gbm_increments(chunk, p.m, seed)\n    p0 = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z0)\n    A0 = mc.payoff_asian(p0, p.k)\n    G0 = mc.payoff_geometric_asian_call(p0, p.k)\n    beta = float(np.cov(A0, G0, ddof=1)[0, 1] / np.var(G0, ddof=1))\n    tot = 0.0\n    ssq = 0.0\n    n_done = 0\n    for c in range(n_ref // chunk):\n        z = mc.gbm_increments(chunk, p.m, seed + 10000 + c)\n        paths = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z)\n        A = mc.payoff_asian(paths, p.k)\n        G = mc.payoff_geometric_asian_call(paths, p.k)\n        cv_i = A - beta * (G - mu_g)\n        tot += float(cv_i.sum())\n        ssq += float((cv_i ** 2).sum())\n        n_done += chunk\n    est = tot / n_done\n    var_cv = (ssq - tot * tot / n_done) / (n_done - 1)\n    se = d * math.sqrt(var_cv / n_done)\n    return float(d * est), float(se)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Convergence experiment\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef convergence_experiment(p, ref_asian: float, rng_seed_base: int = 2000, reps: int = 20):\n    d = math.exp(-p.r * p.t)\n    ref_vanilla = mc.black_scholes_call(p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t)\n    out = {\n        \"N\": [], \"asian_naive\": [], \"asian_antithetic\": [], \"asian_cv\": [], \"vanilla_naive\": [],\n        \"_raw\": {str(N): {\"asian_naive\": [], \"asian_antithetic\": [], \"asian_cv\": [], \"vanilla_naive\": []}\n                 for N in NS_CONVERGENCE},\n    }\n    for N in NS_CONVERGENCE:\n        a_naive, a_anti, a_cv, v_naive = [], [], [], []\n        for r in range(reps):\n            seed = rng_seed_base + r\n            # naive + control variate share one set of paths\n            z = mc.gbm_increments(N, p.m, seed)\n            paths = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z)\n            A = mc.payoff_asian(paths, p.k)\n            G = mc.payoff_geometric_asian_call(paths, p.k)\n            price_naive = d * A.mean()\n            mu_g = mc.geometric_asian_call_price(p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m) / d\n            beta = np.cov(A, G, ddof=1)[0, 1] / np.var(G, ddof=1)\n            price_cv = d * (A.mean() - beta * (G.mean() - mu_g))\n            # vanilla from the same paths\n            vpay = mc.payoff_vanilla(paths, p.k)\n            price_vanilla = d * vpay.mean()\n            # antithetic (paired)\n            za = mc.gbm_increments(N, p.m, seed, antithetic=True)\n            pathsa = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, za)\n            price_anti, _, _ = antithetic_price(pathsa, p.k, p.r, p.t)\n\n            a_naive.append(float(price_naive)); a_cv.append(float(price_cv))\n            v_naive.append(float(price_vanilla)); a_anti.append(float(price_anti))\n\n        out[\"N\"].append(N)\n        out[\"asian_naive\"].append(float(np.sqrt(np.mean((np.array(a_naive) - ref_asian) ** 2))))\n        out[\"asian_cv\"].append(float(np.sqrt(np.mean((np.array(a_cv) - ref_asian) ** 2))))\n        out[\"asian_antithetic\"].append(float(np.sqrt(np.mean((np.array(a_anti) - ref_asian) ** 2))))\n        out[\"vanilla_naive\"].append(float(np.sqrt(np.mean((np.array(v_naive) - ref_vanilla) ** 2))))\n        out[\"_raw\"][str(N)] = {\"asian_naive\": a_naive, \"asian_cv\": a_cv,\n                               \"asian_antithetic\": a_anti, \"vanilla_naive\": v_naive}\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Performance: naive Python loop vs vectorized NumPy (vectorized fn is the hot loop)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef asian_vectorized(z, s0, r, sigma, t, m, k):\n    \"\"\"Vectorized Asian pricer (hot loop for line_profiler). Equivalent to mc.gbm_paths+payoff_asian.\"\"\"\n    dt = t / m\n    drift = (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * dt\n    log_inc = drift + sigma * math.sqrt(dt) * z\n    log_paths = np.concatenate([np.zeros((z.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(log_inc, axis=1)], axis=1)\n    paths = s0 * np.exp(log_paths)\n    avg = paths[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)\n    payoff = np.maximum(avg - k, 0.0)\n    return payoff.mean()\n\n\ndef asian_naive_loop(z, s0, r, sigma, t, m, k):\n    \"\"\"Pure-Python-loop Asian pricer (numpy used only for the pre-drawn RNG array z).\"\"\"\n    dt = t / m\n    drift = (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * dt\n    diff = sigma * math.sqrt(dt)\n    n = z.shape[0]\n    total = 0.0\n    for i in range(n):\n        s = s0\n        ssum = 0.0\n        zi = z[i]\n        for j in range(m):\n            s = s * math.exp(drift + diff * zi[j])\n            ssum += s\n        avg = ssum / m\n        if avg > k:\n            total += avg - k\n    return total / n\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# JSON helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef to_jsonable(x):\n    if isinstance(x, dict):\n        return {str(k): to_jsonable(v) for k, v in x.items()}\n    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):\n        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in x]\n    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):\n        return to_jsonable(x.tolist())\n    if isinstance(x, (np.floating, np.integer)):\n        return x.item()\n    if isinstance(x, (np.bool_,)):\n        return bool(x)\n    if isinstance(x, float):\n        return float(x)\n    if isinstance(x, int):\n        return int(x)\n    return x\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main pipeline\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef parse_args():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Option A: Monte Carlo pricing, variance reduction, Greeks, convergence, performance.\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=42, help=\"primary numpy seed\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--torch-seed\", type=int, default=4242, help=\"independent torch engine seed\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--n-paths\", type=int, default=N_MAIN, help=\"main path count (2^17 default)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--reps\", type=int, default=20, help=\"replication count for VR + convergence\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--outdir\", type=str, default=\"results/approach1/if\", help=\"output directory\")\n    return ap.parse_args()\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    args = parse_args()\n    outdir = Path(args.outdir)\n    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    t_start = time.perf_counter()\n\n    # ---- 0. load params -----------------------------------------------------\n    p = mc.estimate_params()\n    console.print(Panel.fit(\n        f\"[bold cyan]Market parameters[/bold cyan]\\n\"\n        f\"S0 = {p.s0:,.2f}\\nK = {p.k:,.2f}  (at-the-money spot)\\nB = {p.barrier:,.2f}  (1.20 x S0)\\n\"\n        f\"r = {p.r:.5f}  (SHIBOR 1Y)\\nsigma = {p.sigma:.6f}  (5y realized, annualized)\\n\"\n        f\"mu_phys = {p.mu_phys:.6f}  (disclosed only, NOT used in Q pricing)\\n\"\n        f\"T = {p.t}, m = {p.m} steps/yr, dt = {p.dt:.6f}\\n\"\n        f\"window = {p.estimation_window}\\n\"\n        f\"source_last_date = {p.source_last_date}   n_returns = {p.n_returns}\"\n    ))\n    console.print(\"[yellow]Model note:[/yellow] assignment-prescribed GBM with drift r (spot-like); NOT the \"\n                  \"driftless Black-76 futures model. Never conflated; a Black-76 check would be labelled separately.\\n\")\n\n    d = math.exp(-p.r * p.t)\n    n_paths = args.n_paths\n\n    # ---- 1. validation (European vanilla, NumPy vs torch vs BS) --------------\n    z_val = mc.gbm_increments(n_paths, p.m, args.seed)\n    paths_val = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z_val)\n    vpay = mc.payoff_vanilla(paths_val, p.k)\n    mc_np, se_np = mc.mc_price(vpay, p.r, p.t)\n\n    tpaths = torch_simulate(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, n_paths, args.torch_seed)\n    tpay = torch_payoff(\"vanilla\", tpaths, p.k, p.barrier)\n    mc_torch, se_torch = torch_price(tpay, p.r, p.t)\n\n    bs = mc.black_scholes_call(p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t)\n    z_score = (mc_np - bs) / se_np\n    diff_np_torch = abs(mc_np - mc_torch)\n    cross_ok = diff_np_torch <= 3.0 * math.sqrt(se_np ** 2 + se_torch ** 2)\n\n    console.print(Panel(\n        f\"[bold]Validation — European vanilla (N={n_paths})[/bold]\\n\"\n        f\"BS closed form        = {bs:.6f}\\n\"\n        f\"NumPy MC              = {mc_np:.6f}  (SE {se_np:.4f})\\n\"\n        f\"PyTorch MC (seed {args.torch_seed}) = {mc_torch:.6f}  (SE {se_torch:.4f})\\n\"\n        f\"z = (MC_np - BS)/SE   = {z_score:+.3f}   [PASS |z|<=3: {abs(z_score) <= 3}]\\n\"\n        f\"|np - torch|          = {diff_np_torch:.4f}   [PASS <=3*sqrt(se^2+se^2): {cross_ok}]\"\n    ))\n\n    # ---- 2. all four payoffs, both engines -----------------------------------\n    table = Table(title=f\"All four payoffs — NumPy vs PyTorch (N={n_paths})\", header_style=\"bold\")\n    table.add_column(\"Payoff\", justify=\"left\")\n    table.add_column(\"NumPy price\", justify=\"right\")\n    table.add_column(\"NumPy SE\", justify=\"right\")\n    table.add_column(\"PyTorch price\", justify=\"right\")\n    table.add_column(\"PyTorch SE\", justify=\"right\")\n    payoff_results = {}\n    for name in PAYOFFS:\n        pnp = compute_payoff(name, paths_val, p.k, p.barrier)\n        pr_np, se_np2 = mc.mc_price(pnp, p.r, p.t)\n        tpay = torch_payoff(name, tpaths, p.k, p.barrier)\n        pr_t, se_t2 = torch_price(tpay, p.r, p.t)\n        table.add_row(name, f\"{pr_np:.6f}\", f\"{se_np2:.4f}\", f\"{pr_t:.6f}\", f\"{se_t2:.4f}\")\n        payoff_results[name] = {\"numpy\": pr_np, \"numpy_se\": se_np2, \"torch\": pr_t, \"torch_se\": se_t2}\n    console.print(table)\n\n    # ---- 3. Asian variance reduction -----------------------------------------\n    beta, cv_price, cv_se, cv_var, naive_var, vr_cv = asian_control_variate(\n        paths_val, p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m)\n    naive_price, naive_se = mc.mc_price(mc.payoff_asian(paths_val, p.k), p.r, p.t)\n    anti_price, anti_se, anti_var = antithetic_price(\n        mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m,\n                     mc.gbm_increments(n_paths, p.m, args.seed, antithetic=True)),\n        p.k, p.r, p.t)\n    vr_anti = naive_var / anti_var\n\n    # R replications\n    rep_seeds = [1000 + i for i in range(args.reps)]\n    rep = {\"naive\": [], \"anti\": [], \"cv\": [], \"cv_beta\": [],\n           \"naive_var\": [], \"anti_var\": [], \"cv_var\": [], \"vr_anti\": [], \"vr_cv\": []}\n    for s in rep_seeds:\n        z = mc.gbm_increments(n_paths, p.m, s)\n        paths = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z)\n        pr_n, _ = mc.mc_price(mc.payoff_asian(paths, p.k), p.r, p.t)\n        b, pr_c, _, var_c, var_n, vrc = asian_control_variate(paths, p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m)\n        za = mc.gbm_increments(n_paths, p.m, s, antithetic=True)\n        pathsa = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, za)\n        pr_a, _, var_a = antithetic_price(pathsa, p.k, p.r, p.t)\n        rep[\"naive\"].append(pr_n); rep[\"naive_var\"].append(var_n)\n        rep[\"anti\"].append(pr_a); rep[\"anti_var\"].append(var_a)\n        rep[\"cv\"].append(pr_c); rep[\"cv_beta\"].append(b); rep[\"cv_var\"].append(var_c)\n        rep[\"vr_anti\"].append(var_n / var_a); rep[\"vr_cv\"].append(vrc)\n\n    def mstd(x):\n        return float(np.mean(x)), float(np.std(x, ddof=1))\n\n    vr_table = Table(title=\"Asian variance reduction\", header_style=\"bold\")\n    vr_table.add_column(\"Estimator\"); vr_table.add_column(\"price (single)\"); vr_table.add_column(\"SE (single)\")\n    vr_table.add_column(\"price (R=20 mean±std)\"); vr_table.add_column(\"var (R=20 mean±std)\")\n    vr_table.add_column(\"VR vs naive (mean±std)\")\n    vr_table.add_row(\"naive\", f\"{naive_price:.4f}\", f\"{naive_se:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['naive'])[0]:.4f}±{mstd(rep['naive'])[1]:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['naive_var'])[0]:.5f}±{mstd(rep['naive_var'])[1]:.5f}\", \"1.0\")\n    vr_table.add_row(\"antithetic\", f\"{anti_price:.4f}\", f\"{anti_se:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['anti'])[0]:.4f}±{mstd(rep['anti'])[1]:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['anti_var'])[0]:.5f}±{mstd(rep['anti_var'])[1]:.5f}\",\n                     f\"{vr_anti:.3f} ({mstd(rep['vr_anti'])[0]:.3f}±{mstd(rep['vr_anti'])[1]:.3f})\")\n    vr_table.add_row(\"control-variate (geo)\", f\"{cv_price:.4f}\", f\"{cv_se:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['cv'])[0]:.4f}±{mstd(rep['cv'])[1]:.4f}\",\n                     f\"{mstd(rep['cv_var'])[0]:.5f}±{mstd(rep['cv_var'])[1]:.5f}\",\n                     f\"{vr_cv:.2f} ({mstd(rep['vr_cv'])[0]:.2f}±{mstd(rep['vr_cv'])[1]:.2f})\")\n    console.print(vr_table)\n    console.print(f\"[green]CV beta (single run) = {beta:.4f};  geo-Asian closed form = \"\n                  f\"{mc.geometric_asian_call_price(p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m):.4f}[/green]\")\n\n    # ---- 4. Greeks -----------------------------------------------------------\n    bs_delta, bs_vega = bs_greeks(p)\n    z_greeks = mc.gbm_increments(n_paths, p.m, args.seed)\n    paths_base = mc.gbm_paths(p.s0, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, z_greeks)\n\n    greeks = {\"bs\": {\"delta\": bs_delta, \"vega\": bs_vega}, \"pathwise\": {}, \"fd_delta\": {}, \"fd_vega\": {}}\n    # pathwise (vanilla + asian only)\n    for name in [\"vanilla\", \"asian\"]:\n        delta, delta_se, vega, vega_se = pathwise_greeks(paths_base, z_greeks, p, name)\n        greeks[\"pathwise\"][name] = {\"delta\": delta, \"delta_se\": delta_se,\n                                    \"vega\": vega, \"vega_se\": vega_se}\n    # finite differences (all four payoffs)\n    for name in PAYOFFS:\n        greeks[\"fd_delta\"][name] = {}\n        greeks[\"fd_vega\"][name] = {}\n        for frac in DELTA_BUMPS:\n            h = frac * p.s0\n            est, se = fd_greek(name, z_greeks, p, h, \"delta\")\n            greeks[\"fd_delta\"][name][str(frac)] = {\"est\": est, \"se\": se}\n        for eps in VEGA_BUMPS:\n            est, se = fd_greek(name, z_greeks, p, eps, \"vega\")\n            greeks[\"fd_vega\"][name][str(eps)] = {\"est\": est, \"se\": se}\n\n    g_table = Table(title=\"Greeks (vanilla benchmark: BS delta / vega)\", header_style=\"bold\")\n    g_table.add_column(\"Method\"); g_table.add_column(\"delta\"); g_table.add_column(\"delta SE\")\n    g_table.add_column(\"vega\"); g_table.add_column(\"vega SE\")\n    g_table.add_row(\"BS analytic\", f\"{bs_delta:.6f}\", \"-\", f\"{bs_vega:.6f}\", \"-\")\n    for name in [\"vanilla\", \"asian\"]:\n        pw = greeks[\"pathwise\"][name]\n        g_table.add_row(f\"pathwise ({name})\", f\"{pw['delta']:.6f}\", f\"{pw['delta_se']:.5f}\",\n                        f\"{pw['vega']:.6f}\", f\"{pw['vega_se']:.5f}\")\n    for frac in DELTA_BUMPS:\n        fd = greeks[\"fd_delta\"][\"vanilla\"][str(frac)]\n        g_table.add_row(f\"FD delta h={frac}*S0 (vanilla)\", f\"{fd['est']:.6f}\", f\"{fd['se']:.5f}\", \"-\", \"-\")\n    for eps in VEGA_BUMPS:\n        fd = greeks[\"fd_vega\"][\"vanilla\"][str(eps)]\n        g_table.add_row(f\"FD vega eps={eps} (vanilla)\", \"-\", \"-\", f\"{fd['est']:.6f}\", f\"{fd['se']:.5f}\")\n    console.print(g_table)\n    console.print(Panel(\n        \"[bold]Bias-variance discussion[/bold]\\n\"\n        \"Pathwise Greeks apply only to a.s. differentiable payoffs (vanilla, arithmetic Asian). The \"\n        \"digital and up-and-out barrier payoffs are discontinuous in S (indicator / barrier step), so the \"\n        \"naive pathwise (score-function) derivative is ill-defined at the discontinuity and the estimator \"\n        \"degenerates to a boundary term; only finite differences are reported for those two payoffs.\\n\"\n        f\"Vanilla delta FD vs BS analytic: small-h FD is near-unbiased but noisy (large SE); large-h FD is \"\n        f\"stable but biased. Pathwise vanilla delta/vega is unbiased with SE comparable to the price SE.\\n\"\n        f\"{CVAR_NOTE}.\"\n    ))\n\n    # ---- 5. convergence If antithetic, n_paths must be even;\n138:     the second half is the negation of the first half (paired rows).\"\"\"\n139:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n140:     if antithetic:\n141:         if n_paths % 2 != 0:\n142:             raise ValueError(\"antithetic requires an even number of paths\")\n143:         half = rng.standard_normal((n_paths // 2, m))\n144:         return np.concatenate([half, -half], axis=0)\n145:     return rng.standard_normal((n_paths, m))\n146: \n147: \n148: def gbm_paths(s0: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float, m: int, z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n149:     \"\"\"Simulate paths from increments Z. Returns array of shape (n_paths, m + 1), paths[:, 0] == s0.\"\"\"\n150:     dt = t / m\n151:     drift = (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * dt\n152:     diffusion = sigma * math.sqrt(dt) * z\n153:     log_increments = drift + diffusion\n154:     log_paths = np.concatenate([np.zeros((z.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(log_increments, axis=1)], axis=1)\n155:     return s0 * np.exp(log_paths)\n156: \n157: \n158: def simulate_gbm(s0: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float, m: int,\n159:                  n_paths: int, seed: int, antithetic: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:\n160:     z = gbm_increments(n_paths, m, seed, antithetic=antithetic)\n161:     return gbm_paths(s0, r, sigma, t, m, z)\n162: \n163: \n164: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n165: # Payoffs (monitored on t_1..t_m; S_0 NOT monitored)\n166: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n167: \n168: def payoff_vanilla(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n169:     return np.maximum(paths[:, -1] - k, 0.0)\n170: \n171: \n172: def payoff_asian(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n173:     return np.maximum(paths[:, 1:].mean(axis=1) - k, 0.0)\n174: \n175: \n176: def payoff_barrier(paths: np.ndarray, k: float, b: float) -> np.ndarray:\n177:     monitored = paths[:, 1:]\n178:     alive = monitored.max(axis=1) < b\n179:     return np.maximum(paths[:, -1] - k, 0.0) * alive\n180: \n181: \n182: def payoff_digital(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n183:     return (paths[:, -1] > k).astype(np.float64)\n184: \n185: \n186: def geometric_average(paths: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n187:     return np.exp(np.log(paths[:, 1:]).mean(axis=1))\n188: \n189: \n190: def payoff_geometric_asian_call(paths: np.ndarray, k: float) -> np.ndarray:\n191:     return np.maximum(geometric_average(paths) - k, 0.0)\n192: \n193: \n194: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n195: # Black-Scholes closed form + discrete-grid geometric Asian closed form\n196: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n197: \n198: def black_scholes_call(s0: float, k: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:\n199:     d1 = (math.log(s0 / k) + (r + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * t) / (sigma * math.sqrt(t))\n200:     d2 = d1 - sigma * math.sqrt(t)\n201:     return s0 * norm.cdf(d1) - k * math.exp(-r * t) * norm.cdf(d2)\n202: \n203: \n204: def geometric_asian_moments(s0: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float, m: int):\n205:     \"\"\"Exact moments of the discrete geometric average over t_i = i*T/m, i=1..m, under Q.\"\"\"\n206:     mu_g = math.log(s0) + (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * t * (m + 1) / (2 * m)\n207:     var_g = sigma * sigma * t * t * (m + 1) * (2 * m + 1) / (6 * m * m)\n208:     return mu_g, var_g\n209: \n210: \n211: def geometric_asian_call_price(s0: float, k: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float, m: int) -> float:\n212:     mu_g, var_g = geometric_asian_moments(s0, r, sigma, t, m)\n213:     sd = math.sqrt(var_g)\n214:     d1 = (mu_g - math.log(k) + var_g) / sd\n215:     d2 = d1 - sd\n216:     eg = math.exp(mu_g + var_g / 2.0)\n217:     return math.exp(-r * t) * (eg * norm.cdf(d1) - k * norm.cdf(d2))\n218: \n219: \n220: def mc_price(payoff: np.ndarray, r: float, t: float):\n221:     \"\"\"Return (discounted mean price, standard error of that price).\"\"\"\n222:     disc = math.exp(-r * t)\n223:     n = payoff.shape[0]\n224:     mean = float(payoff.mean())\n225:     se = float(payoff.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n)) * disc\n226:     return disc * mean, se\n227: \n228: \n229: def save_json(obj, path: Path) -> None:\n230:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n231:     path.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))"

Good.\n\nNow the functions:\n\n```python\ndef set_seed(seed):\n    torch.manual_seed(seed)\n    np.random.seed(seed)\n```\n\nTorch GBM:\n```python\ndef gbm_paths_torch(s0, r, sigma, t, m, n_paths, seed, dtype=torch.float64):\n    torch.manual_seed(seed)\n    dt = t / m\n    drift = (r - 0.5*sigma*sigma)*dt\n    vol = sigma*math.sqrt(dt)\n    Z = torch.randn((n_paths, m), dtype=dtype)  # note: after manual_seed, deterministic\n    log_inc = drift + vol*Z\n    log_paths = torch.cat([torch.zeros((n_paths,1), dtype=dtype), torch.cumsum(log_inc, dim=1)], dim=1)\n    return s0*torch.exp(log_paths)\n```\n\nWait, drift is a float (Python) not tensor — but `drift + vol*Z` will broadcast fine since drift is scalar Python float. Fine.\n\nTorch MC price check:\n```python\ndef torch_mc_price(paths, k, r, t):\n    payoff = torch.clamp(paths[:, -1] - k, min=0.0)\n    disc = math.exp(-r*t)\n    n = payoff.shape[0]\n    mean = float(payoff.mean())\n    se = float(payoff.std(unbiased=True).item() / math.sqrt(n)) * disc\n    return disc*mean, se\n```\n\nPayoff: H(S) = max(S_T - K, 0).\n\nMLP:\n```python\nclass HedgeMLP(nn.Module):\n    def __init__(self, hidden=(64,64,64)):\n        super().__init__()\n        layers = []\n        prev = 2\n        for h in hidden:\n            layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, h))\n            layers.append(nn.ReLU())\n            prev = h\n        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, 1))\n        self.net = nn.Sequential(*layers)\n    def forward(self, x):\n        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)  # (...,)\n```\n\nInput x = [S/S0, t/T]. Note i=0 gives t_frac=0, s_ratio=1.0.\n\nHedging P&L (vectorized, torch):\n```python\ndef hedge_pnl(S, delta, k, r, dt, m, kappa):\n    # S: (n_paths, m+1) float; delta: (n_paths, m)\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    dS = S[:, 1:] - S[:, :-1]  # (n_paths, m)\n    i = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype)\n    discount = torch.exp(r * (m - i) * dt)  # (m,)\n    hedge_gain = (delta * dS * discount).sum(dim=1)  # (n_paths,)\n    # cost\n    delta_prev = torch.cat([torch.zeros((n,1), device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype), delta[:, :-1]], dim=1)\n    S_spot = S[:, :-1]  # decision-time spot S_i, i=0..m-1\n    cost = kappa * (delta - delta_prev).abs() * S_spot\n    total_cost = cost.sum(dim=1)\n    payoff = torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - k, min=0.0)\n    V = hedge_gain - total_cost - payoff\n    return V, total_cost, (delta - delta_prev).abs().sum(dim=1)  # turnover\n```\n\nWait turnover: Σ|Δ_i - Δ_{i-1}|. 1) // batch_size\n    for epoch in range(1, epochs+1):\n        model.train()\n        perm = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)\n        total_loss = 0.0\n        for b in range(n_batches):\n            idx = perm[b*batch_size:(b+1)*batch_size]\n            S_batch = S_train[idx]\n            L = policy_loss(S_batch, model, k, s0, r, t, m, dt, kappa)\n            loss = eta + (1.0/(1-alpha)) * torch.relu(L - This module only implements the Option-B deep-hedging\npipeline (single self-contained script, argparse, linear load -> simulate -> fit -> evaluate ->\nwrite outputs), per the assignment §4.4 and the AGENTS.md Option-B contract.\n\nAccounting conventions (documented here AND in metrics.json, and echoed in the terminal):\n  * Hedging grid t_i = i*dt, i = 0..m-1, m = 252 steps, dt = T/m = 1/252.  S_i denotes S_{t_i}.\n    The path array holds S_0..S_m (m+1 points); S_0 is the initial spot, NOT a decision point.\n  * Delta_i is DECIDED at t_i from information available at t_i only: for the neural policy\n    f_theta(S_{t_i}/S_0, t_i/T); for Black-Scholes delta N(d1(S_{t_i}, T - t_i)) at rebalance dates.\n  * Terminal hedging P&L (assignment formula, exactly as written):\n        V_T = sum_{i=0}^{m-1} exp(r*(T - t_i)) * Delta_i * (S_{i+1} - S_i)\n            - kappa * sum_{i=0}^{m-1} |Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}| * S_{t_i}\n            - H(S_T),   with Delta_{-1} := 0 (the initial position is charged), H = max(S_T-K,0).\n    Note the discount factor uses the DECISION time t_i (assignment's simplified cash-flow timing:\n    the increment S_{i+1}-S_i actually accrues over [t_i, t_{i+1}] but is compounded from t_i, not\n    t_{i+1}).  We implement it exactly as written rather than silently altering it.\n  * Transaction cost is charged at the decision-time spot S_{t_i}, proportional to |DeltaDelta|,\n    summed over i = 0..m-1.  There is NO extra terminal close-out term: the final hedge P&L\n    realizes the last move (i = m-1) inside the sum, matching the assignment formula.\n  * Premium convention: the option premium is EXCLUDED from V_T exactly as the assignment writes\n    it.  Adding the constant premium e^{rT}*C_BS would shift mean P&L and CVaR equally for EVERY\n    policy, so it changes no comparison and leaves variance/turnover unchanged; we therefore omit\n    it and note this.  (Consequently a good delta hedge has E[V_T] ~ e^{rT}*C_BS > 0.)\n  * The SAME accounting applies to the neural policy and to every Black-Scholes baseline.\n\nRisk measure: L = -V_T; CVaR_0.95 of L is minimised via Rockafellar-Uryasev\n    min_{theta, eta}  eta + (1/(1-alpha)) * mean(relu(L_theta - eta)),   alpha = 0.95.\nEvaluation CVaR is computed independently of the training loss (sort L descending, mean of the\nworst 5%) on held-out paths.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport gc\nimport json\nimport math\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport torch\nimport torch.nn as nn\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nsys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / \"code\"))\n\nimport mc_common as mc  # noqa: E402  (authoritative shared mathematics)\n\nimport plotly.graph_objects as go  # noqa: E402\nfrom rich.console import Console  # noqa: E402\nfrom rich.panel import Panel  # noqa: E402\nfrom rich.table import Table  # noqa: E402\n\nALPHA = 0.95\nDEVICE = \"cpu\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:\n    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Option B deep hedging (European vanilla call, IF).\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=42, help=\"global seed (default 42)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--n-train\", type=int, default=131072, help=\"training paths (default 2^17)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--n-val\", type=int, default=32768, help=\"validation paths\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--n-test\", type=int, default=32768, help=\"test paths\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--hidden\", type=int, nargs=\"+\", default=[64, 64, 64],\n                   help=\"MLP hidden layer widths (<=3 layers)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--lr\", type=float, default=1e-3, help=\"Adam learning rate\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--epochs\", type=int, default=60, help=\"max epochs\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--batch-size\", type=int, default=4096, help=\"minibatch size (paths)\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--patience\", type=int, default=12, help=\"early-stopping patience\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--min-delta\", type=float, default=1e-4, help=\"early-stopping min delta\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--train-kappa\", type=float, default=0.001,\n                   help=\"transaction cost (decimal) the neural policy is trained at\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--device\", type=str, default=DEVICE)\n    return p.parse_args()\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Seeding / GBM simulation (PyTorch)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef gbm_paths_torch(s0: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float, m: int,\n                    n_paths: int, seed: int, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Risk-neutral GBM paths under Q, exactly as mc_common (drift r, not Black-76).\n\n    Returns (n_paths, m+1) with paths[:, 0] == s0.\n    \"\"\"\n    torch.manual_seed(seed)\n    dt = t / m\n    drift = (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * dt\n    vol = sigma * math.sqrt(dt)\n    z = torch.randn((n_paths, m), dtype=dtype)\n    log_inc = drift + vol * z\n    log_paths = torch.cat([torch.zeros((n_paths, 1), dtype=dtype),\n                           torch.cumsum(log_inc, dim=1)], dim=1)\n    return s0 * torch.exp(log_paths)\n\n\ndef torch_mc_price(paths: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float, t: float):\n    \"\"\"Return (discounted mean price, standard error) for the vanilla call on given paths.\"\"\"\n    payoff = torch.clamp(paths[:, -1] - k, min=0.0)\n    disc = math.exp(-r * t)\n    n = payoff.shape[0]\n    mean = float(payoff.mean().item())\n    se = float(payoff.std(unbiased=True).item() / math.sqrt(n)) * disc\n    return disc * mean, se\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Neural hedging policy (MLP, <= 3 hidden layers)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nclass HedgeMLP(nn.Module):\n    def __init__(self, hidden=(64, 64, 64)):\n        super().__init__()\n        assert len(hidden) <= 3, \"at most three hidden layers\"\n        layers = []\n        prev = 2\n        for h in hidden:\n            layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, h))\n            layers.append(nn.ReLU())\n            prev = h\n        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev, 1))\n        self.net = nn.Sequential(*layers)\n\n    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n        # x: (..., 2) -> delta (...,)\n        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)\n\n\ndef policy_inputs(S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, m: int) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Stack (S_{t_i}/S_0, t_i/T) for i = 0..m-1 into a (n_paths*m, 2) tensor.\n\n    Causal: only S at time t_i (and the calendar time t_i) enter the feature vector.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    s_spot = S[:, :-1]  # (n, m) decision-time spots\n    s_ratio = s_spot / s0\n    t_frac = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype) / m\n    x = torch.stack([s_ratio, t_frac.expand(n, m)], dim=-1)  # (n, m, 2)\n    return x.reshape(-1, 2)\n\n\ndef neural_delta(model: HedgeMLP, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, m: int) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Return delta (n_paths, m): Delta_i = f_theta(S_{t_i}/S_0, t_i/T).\"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    x = policy_inputs(S, s0, m)\n    return model(x).reshape(n, m)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Hedging P&L (assignment formula, shared by neural and BS policies)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef hedge_pnl(S: torch.Tensor, delta: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float,\n              dt: float, m: int, kappa: float):\n    \"\"\"Terminal hedging P&L per the assignment formula.\n\n    Args:\n        S:      (n_paths, m+1) asset path, S[:, 0] == S_0.\n        delta:  (n_paths, m) position Delta_i decided at t_i.\n    Returns:\n        V:          (n_paths,) terminal P&L (premium excluded).\n        turnover:   (n_paths,) sum_i |Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}|.\n        cost:       (n_paths,) kappa * sum_i |Delta_i - Delta_{i-1}| * S_{t_i}.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    dS = S[:, 1:] - S[:, :-1]                    # (n, m)  S_{i+1} - S_i\n    i = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype)\n    discount = torch.exp(r * (m - i) * dt)       # (m,)  exp(r*(T - t_i))\n    hedge_gain = (delta * dS * discount).sum(dim=1)\n\n    delta_prev = torch.cat([torch.zeros((n, 1), device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype),\n                            delta[:, :-1]], dim=1)   # Delta_{i-1}, Delta_{-1} = 0\n    s_spot = S[:, :-1]                           # decision-time spot S_{t_i}\n    trade = (delta - delta_prev).abs()\n    cost = kappa * (trade * s_spot).sum(dim=1)\n    turnover = trade.sum(dim=1)\n\n    payoff = torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - k, min=0.0)  # H(S_T) = max(S_T - K, 0)\n    V = hedge_gain - cost - payoff\n    return V, turnover, cost\n\n\ndef empirical_cvar(loss: torch.Tensor, alpha: float = ALPHA) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Empirical CVaR_alpha of a loss vector (independent of the R-U training loss).\n\n    Sort descending, average the worst (1-alpha) fraction (the upper tail of L).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = loss.numel()\n    k = max(1, int(round((1 - alpha) * n)))\n    sorted_desc, _ = torch.sort(loss, descending=True)\n    return float(sorted_desc[:k].mean().item())\n\n\ndef policy_loss(model: HedgeMLP, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, k: float, r: float,\n                dt: float, m: int, kappa: float) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"L = -V_T for the neural policy on paths S (loss, larger is worse).\"\"\"\n    delta = neural_delta(model, S, s0, m)\n    V, _, _ = hedge_pnl(S, delta, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n    return -V\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Black-Scholes delta benchmark\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef bs_delta(S_spot: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float, sigma: float,\n             tau: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"N(d1) with d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + sigma^2/2)*tau) / (sigma*sqrt(tau)).\"\"\"\n    d1 = (torch.log(S_spot / k) + (r + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * tau) / (sigma * torch.sqrt(tau))\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + torch.erf(d1 / math.sqrt(2.0)))\n\n\ndef bs_delta_hedge(S: torch.Tensor, k: float, r: float, sigma: float, t: float,\n                   m: int, freq: int) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"BS-delta positions (n_paths, m), rebalanced every `freq` steps and held in between.\n\n    Trades occur ONLY at rebalance dates i in {0, freq, 2*freq, ...}; between those dates the\n    position is held constant (no trade, no cost).  Cost is still charged on |DeltaDelta| at the\n    rebalance dates via the shared hedge_pnl (which uses Delta_{i-1}).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S.shape[0]\n    dt = t / m\n    i = torch.arange(m, device=S.device, dtype=S.dtype)\n    tau = (m - i) * dt                       # remaining time at each potential rebalance point\n    s_spot = S[:, :-1]\n    target = bs_delta(s_spot, k, r, sigma, tau)   # full target delta at every step (cheap)\n    rebalance_col = (i // freq) * freq        # last rebalance index <= i\n    return target[:, rebalance_col]           # (n, m) held-constant positions\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Training (Rockafellar-Uryasev CVaR)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef train_model(model: HedgeMLP, eta: nn.Parameter, S_train: torch.Tensor, S_val: torch.Tensor,\n                s0: float, k: float, r: float, dt: float, m: int, kappa: float, alpha: float,\n                lr: float, epochs: int, batch_size: int, patience: int, min_delta: float,\n                shuffle_seed: int, console: Console):\n    n = S_train.shape[0]\n    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(list(model.parameters()) + [eta], lr=lr)\n    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(shuffle_seed)\n    n_batches = (n + batch_size - 1) // batch_size\n    n_train_eval = min(n, 32768)          # fixed subset for per-epoch train CVaR reporting\n    S_train_eval = S_train[:n_train_eval]\n\n    history = {\"epoch\": [], \"train_loss\": [], \"train_cvar\": [], \"val_cvar\": []}\n    best_val_cvar = float(\"inf\")\n    best_state, best_eta = None, None\n    epochs_no_improve = 0\n    rho = 1.0 / (1.0 - alpha)             # = 20\n\n    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):\n        model.train()\n        perm = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)\n        total_loss = 0.0\n        for b in range(n_batches):\n            idx = perm[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]\n            S_batch = S_train[idx]\n            L = policy_loss(model, S_batch, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            loss = eta + rho * torch.relu(L - eta).mean()\n            optimizer.zero_grad()\n            loss.backward()\n            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(list(model.parameters()) + [eta], 10.0)\n            optimizer.step()\n            total_loss += float(loss.item()) * int(idx.numel())\n\n        avg_train_loss = total_loss / n\n        model.eval()\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            L_train = policy_loss(model, S_train_eval, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            train_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_train, alpha)\n            L_val = policy_loss(model, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            val_cvar = empirical_cvar(L_val, alpha)\n\n        history[\"epoch\"].append(epoch)\n        history[\"train_loss\"].append(avg_train_loss)\n        history[\"train_cvar\"].append(train_cvar)\n        history[\"val_cvar\"].append(val_cvar)\n\n        if epoch == 1 or epoch % 5 == 0:\n            console.print(\n                f\"[cyan]epoch {epoch:3d}[/]  train_loss={avg_train_loss:8.4f}  \"\n                f\"train_cvar={train_cvar:9.4f}  val_cvar={val_cvar:9.4f}\")\n\n        if val_cvar < best_val_cvar - min_delta:\n            best_val_cvar = val_cvar\n            epochs_no_improve = 0\n            best_state = {kk: vv.detach().clone() for kk, vv in model.state_dict().items()}\n            best_eta = eta.detach().clone()\n        else:\n            epochs_no_improve += 1\n            if epochs_no_improve >= patience:\n                console.print(f\"[yellow]early stopping at epoch {epoch} \"\n                              f\"(no improvement > {min_delta} for {patience} epochs)[/]\")\n                break\n\n    if best_state is not None:\n        model.load_state_dict(best_state)\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            eta.copy_(best_eta)\n\n    return history, best_val_cvar\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Evaluation helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef evaluate_policy(delta_fn, S: torch.Tensor, s0: float, k: float, r: float,\n                    dt: float, m: int, kappa: float, alpha: float):\n    \"\"\"Return a dict of summary statistics for one (policy, kappa) on paths S.\"\"\"\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        delta = delta_fn(S)\n        V, turnover, cost = hedge_pnl(S, delta, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n        L = -V\n        return {\n            \"mean_pnl\": float(V.mean().item()),\n            \"var_pnl\": float(V.var(unbiased=True).item()),\n            \"cvar95\": empirical_cvar(L, alpha),\n            \"turnover\": float(turnover.mean().item()),\n            \"avg_cost\": float(cost.mean().item()),\n        }\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# main\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef main() -> None:\n    args = parse_args()\n    console = Console()\n    torch.set_num_threads(max(1, torch.get_num_threads()))\n\n    p = mc.estimate_params()\n    s0, k, r, sigma, t, m, dt = p.s0, p.k, p.r, p.sigma, p.t, p.m, p.dt\n    assert abs(k - s0) < 1e-12, \"K must equal S0 (at-the-money spot)\"\n\n    console.print(Panel.fit(\n        f\"[bold]Deep hedging — European vanilla call on IF[/]\\n\"\n        f\"S0 = {s0:.2f}   K = {k:.2f} (ATM)   r = {r:.5f}   sigma = {sigma:.5f}\\n\"\n        f\"T = {t}   m = {m} steps   dt = {dt:.6f}   alpha = {ALPHA}   kappa_train = {args.train_kappa}\",\n        title=\"Parameters (mc_common.estimate_params)\"))\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 2. Simulation & independent torch/numpy/BS price check (seed 42)\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    console.print(\"[bold]Simulating paths and verifying torch vs numpy vs Black-Scholes...[/]\")\n    bs_price = mc.black_scholes_call(s0, k, r, sigma, t)\n\n    # NumPy MC (seed 42), float64 — then release.\n    np_paths = mc.simulate_gbm(s0, r, sigma, t, m, args.n_train, 42)\n    np_price, np_se = mc.mc_price(mc.payoff_vanilla(np_paths, k), r, t)\n    del np_paths\n    gc.collect()\n\n    # PyTorch MC (seed 42), float64 — independent draws (torch.manual_seed != numpy default_rng).\n    paths_torch64 = gbm_paths_torch(s0, r, sigma, t, m, args.n_train, 42, dtype=torch.float64)\n    torch_price, torch_se = torch_mc_price(paths_torch64, k, r, t)\n    del paths_torch64\n    gc.collect()\n\n    z_bs = (torch_price - bs_price) / torch_se\n    z_cross = (torch_price - np_price) / math.sqrt(torch_se ** 2 + np_se ** 2)\n\n    console.print(Table(\n        \"check\", \"value\", \"SE\", \"z\", title=\"Vanilla call price cross-check (seed 42)\"))\n    # (populated below in a cleaner single table)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Main float32 simulation (train/val/test, independent seeds)\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    S_train = gbm_paths_torch(s0, r, sigma, t, m, args.n_train, 42, dtype=torch.float32)\n    S_val = gbm_paths_torch(s0, r, sigma, t, m, args.n_val, 123, dtype=torch.float32)\n    S_test = gbm_paths_torch(s0, r, sigma, t, m, args.n_test, 2026, dtype=torch.float32)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Model\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    model = HedgeMLP(hidden=tuple(args.hidden)).to(args.device)\n    eta = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.0))\n    n_params = sum(pp.numel() for pp in model.parameters())\n    console.print(f\"[bold]MLP policy[/] hidden={tuple(args.hidden)}  params={n_params}  \"\n                  f\"(input: S/S0 and t/T; <= 3 hidden layers, causal)\")\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 3. Train\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    console.print(f\"[bold]Training[/] N_train={args.n_train} N_val={args.n_val} lr={args.lr} \"\n                  f\"batch={args.batch_size} max_epochs={args.epochs} kappa={args.train_kappa}\")\n    t0 = time.perf_counter()\n    history, best_val_cvar = train_model(\n        model, eta, S_train, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, args.train_kappa, ALPHA,\n        args.lr, args.epochs, args.batch_size, args.patience, args.min_delta,\n        args.seed, console)\n    fit_seconds = time.perf_counter() - t0\n    n_epochs_run = len(history[\"epoch\"])\n    console.print(f\"[bold]Training done[/] {n_epochs_run} epochs in {fit_seconds:.1f}s \"\n                  f\"best_val_cvar={best_val_cvar:.4f}\")\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 4. Evaluation on held-out test/val (neural at 3 kappa, BS at 9 combos)\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    kappas = [(0.0, \"0bp\"), (0.001, \"10bp\"), (0.005, \"50bp\")]\n    freqs = [1, 5, 21]\n\n    def neural_delta_fn(S):\n        return neural_delta(model, S, s0, m)\n\n    rows = {}   # name -> summary dict\n    # Neural policy: every-step rebalancing, evaluated at the three cost levels.\n    for kv, label in kappas:\n        rows[f\"neural_{label}\"] = {\"test\": evaluate_policy(\n            neural_delta_fn, S_test, s0, k, r, dt, m, kv, ALPHA)}\n        rows[f\"neural_{label}\"][\"val\"] = evaluate_policy(\n            neural_delta_fn, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, kv, ALPHA)\n\n    # BS delta: 3 frequencies x 3 costs.\n    for fq in freqs:\n        def bs_fn(S, fq=fq):\n            return bs_delta_hedge(S, k, r, sigma, t, m, fq)\n        for kv, label in kappas:\n            name = f\"bs_f{fq}_{label}\"\n            rows[name] = {\"test\": evaluate_policy(bs_fn, S_test, s0, k, r, dt, m, kv, ALPHA)}\n            rows[name][\"val\"] = evaluate_policy(bs_fn, S_val, s0, k, r, dt, m, kv, ALPHA)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 5. Figures\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    out_dir = ROOT / \"results\" / \"approach2\" / \"if\"\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    epochs = history[\"epoch\"]\n    fig = go.Figure()\n    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=epochs, y=history[\"train_cvar\"], name=\"train CVaR95\"))\n    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=epochs, y=history[\"val_cvar\"], name=\"val CVaR95\"))\n    fig.update_layout(title=\"Deep-hedging training curve (CVaR95 of L=-V_T)\",\n                      xaxis_title=\"epoch\", yaxis_title=\"CVaR95\")\n    fig.write_html(str(out_dir / \"training_curve.html\"), include_plotlyjs=True)\n\n    # P&L distribution (test): neural @10bp vs a few BS baselines.\n    with torch.no_grad():\n        V_neural = -policy_loss(model, S_test, s0, k, r, dt, m, 0.001).detach().cpu().numpy()\n        V_bs1_0 = hedge_pnl(S_test, bs_delta_hedge(S_test, k, r, sigma, t, m, 1), k, r, dt, m, 0.0)[0].numpy()\n        V_bs1_10 = hedge_pnl(S_test, bs_delta_hedge(S_test, k, r, sigma, t, m, 1), k, r, dt, m, 0.001)[0].numpy()\n        V_bs21_0 = hedge_pnl(S_test, bs_delta_hedge(S_test, k, r, sigma, t, m, 21), k, r, dt, m, 0.0)[0].numpy()\n\n    fig = go.Figure()\n    for arr, name in [(V_neural, \"neural @10bp\"), (V_bs1_0, \"BS 1d @0bp\"),\n                      (V_bs1_10, \"BS 1d @10bp\"), (V_bs21_0, \"BS 21d @0bp\")]:\n        fig.add_trace(go.Histogram(x=arr, name=name, histnorm=\"probability density\",\n                                   opacity=0.6, nbinsx=120))\n    fig.update_layout(title=\"Test P&L distribution (V_T, premium excluded)\", barmode=\"overlay\",\n                      xaxis_title=\"V_T\", yaxis_title=\"density\")\n    fig.write_html(str(out_dir / \"pnl_distribution.html\"), include_plotlyjs=True)\n\n    # CVaR95 bar chart across all methods (test).\n    names = list(rows.keys())\n    cvar_test = [rows[nn][\"test\"][\"cvar95\"] for nn in names]\n    fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=names, y=cvar_test, marker_color=[\n        \"#1f77b4\" if nn.startswith(\"neural\") else \"#ff7f0e\" for nn in names]))\n    fig.update_layout(title=\"Test CVaR95 of L = -V_T across strategies\",\n                      xaxis_title=\"strategy\", yaxis_title=\"CVaR95\")\n    fig.write_html(str(out_dir / \"benchmark_bars.html\"), include_plotlyjs=True)\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # 6. metrics.json\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    params = dict(p.to_dict())\n    params.update({\n        \"seed\": args.seed,\n        \"n_train\": args.n_train,\n        \"n_val\": args.n_val,\n        \"n_test\": args.n_test,\n        \"hidden\": list(args.hidden),\n We recompute\n        eta = quantile_alpha(L_theta) on a fixed training subset at the START of every epoch.\n      * For fixed eta, we take Adam gradient steps on theta through\n        eta + rho * mean(relu(L_theta - eta)); only the paths with L > eta (the upper tail)\n        contribute gradient.\n\n    A purely gradient-based update of eta is NOT used because Adam normalises the update\n    magnitude to ~lr per step, so eta would track the VaR far too slowly (the VaR drops by\n    O(10^3) points as the policy learns to hedge); the exact quantile step sidesteps this.\n    \"\"\"\n    n = S_train.shape[0]\n    n_train_eval = min(n, 32768)\n    S_train_eval = S_train[:n_train_eval]\n    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)\n    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(shuffle_seed)\n    n_batches = (n + batch_size - 1) // batch_size\n    rho = 1.0 / (1.0 - alpha)\n\n    def current_var_alpha() -> float:\n        model.eval()\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            L = policy_loss(model, S_train_eval, s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            return float(torch.quantile(L, alpha).item())\n\n    history = {\"epoch\": [], \"train_loss\": [], \"train_cvar\": [], \"val_cvar\": [], \"eta\": []}\n    best_val_cvar = float(\"inf\")\n    best_state, best_eta = None, None\n    epochs_no_improve = 0\n\n    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):\n        eta_q = current_var_alpha()\n        eta.data.fill_(eta_q)              # exact R-U minimiser in eta (VaR_alpha)\n\n        model.train()\n        perm = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)\n        total_loss = 0.0\n        for b in range(n_batches):\n            idx = perm[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]\n            L = policy_loss(model, S_train[idx], s0, k, r, dt, m, kappa)\n            loss = eta_q + rho * torch.relu(L - No-arbitrage verification, reported per expiry and per date:\n136:    butterfly (Gatheral): $g(k) = \\Big(1 - \\frac{k\\,w'(k)}{2w(k)}\\Big)^2 - \\frac{w'(k)^2}{4}\\Big(\\frac{1}{w(k)} + \\frac14\\Big) \\ge 0$;\n137:    calendar: $w_{T_2}(k) \\ge w_{T_1}(k)$ for $T_2 > T_1$; violations counted and located, not silently dropped.\n138: 3. Data and calibration\n14: \n15: ### 2.1 Sources and provenance (see `data/metadata.json`)\n16: \n17: | Artefact | Source | Rows | Range |\n18: |---|---|---|---|\n19: | `data/clean/if_main.csv` | AKShare `futures_main_sina` → Sina Finance; IF main continuous contract | 2374 | 2017-01-17 … 2026-11-02 |\n20: | `data/clean/csi300_index.csv` | AKShare `index_zh_a_hist` → Eastmoney; CSI 300 index (000300) | 2386 | 2017-01-03 … 2026-11-03 |\n21: | `data/clean/shibor.csv` | AKShare `macro_china_shibor_all` → CFETS/Eastmoney; SHIBOR all tenors | 2396 | 2017-03-17 … 2026-11-03 |\n22: \n23: All three artefacts are committed (total < 0.5 MB) with SHA-256 hashes recorded in `data/metadata.json`; `uv run python data/fetch.py --verify-only` re-checks them offline and `--refresh` re-downloads. FastboxData credentials were not used; the public AKShare route was used instead, as permitted by the assignment (\"`ak.futures_main_sina`\").\n24: \n25: **Roll convention.** The IF0 series is AKShare's main-contract continuous series (dominant contract by volume/open interest). Roll gaps can induce artificial jumps in price *levels*; all estimation below uses **log returns**, which are roll-gap tolerant in practice but we flag that returns straddling rolls may embed small artefacts. No back-adjustment is applied; the series is used as displayed by the vendor.\n26: \n27: ### 2.2 Estimation window and parameters\n28: \n29: * **Window:** trailing 5 calendar years, **2021-10-28 … 2026-11-02**, n = 1214 daily log returns of IF0 close. (Full history 2017–2026 was retrieved; the 5-year window matches the assignment's \"≥ 5 years\" requirement and avoids mixing pre-2021 regimes.)\n30: * **Physical drift (disclosure only):** μ̂ = mean(log-return) × 252 ≈ **−4.24 % p.a.** (not used in risk-neutral pricing).\n31: * **Volatility (used for pricing):** σ̂ = std(log-returns, ddof=1) × √252 ≈ **19.07 % p.a.** (full-sample 2017–2026: ≈ 20.08 %, reported for reference).\n32: * **Discount rate:** SHIBOR 1Y fixing 2026-11-03 = **1.4390 % p.a.** → r = 0.01439, flat for T = 1Y. No curve interpolation is required at this tenor; for other tenors we would linearly interpolate SHIBOR fixings in the rate (not in the discount factor).\n33: * **Spot:** S0 = **3974.8** (IF0 close 2026-11-02). **Strike:** K = S0 (spot-ATM). **Barrier:** B = 1.20 × S0 = 4769.76. **Maturity:** T = 1.0 y, **m = 252** monitors/year, dt = T/m.\n34: \n35: ### 2.3 Model distinction (important)\n36: \n37: The assignment prescribes simulation of the *futures price* with the GBM\n38: \n39: S(t+dt) = S(t) · exp[(r − σ²/2)·dt + σ·√dt·Z],  Z ~ N(0,1) i.i.d.\n40: \n41: We implement exactly this for its Black–Scholes validation. Under standard risk-neutral theory a **futures price** is driftless (Black-76: dF = σ F dW̃). We deliberately do **not** silently conflate the two: the assignment-prescribed GBM-on-futures is used throughout, Black–Scholes-with-drift-r is its closed-form benchmark, and if a Black-76 cross-check is reported it is labelled separately as such. Physical-measure market risk (real-world drift, jump behaviour) is out of scope; our CVaR figures are **model-implied** under the risk-neutral simulator.\n42: \n43: ## 3. Mathematical specification\n44: \n45: ### 3.1 Exact GBM simulation (both engines)\n46: \n47: With t_i = i·dt, log S_{t_i} = log S0 + Σ_{j<i} [(r − σ²/2)dt + σ√dt Z_j]; paths[:,0] = S0. NumPy engine: `np.random.default_rng(seed)`. PyTorch engine: `torch.Generator` (CPU), same recursion, independent seed (4242 in the cross-engine check; 42 elsewhere). Minimum 252 steps/year as prescribed. Antithetic sampling uses pairs (Z, −Z) with an even number of paths.\n48: \n49: ### 3.2 Payoffs (monitored on t_1..t_m; **S_0 is NOT monitored**)\n50: \n51: 1. Arithmetic Asian call: A = max(mean(S_{t_1..m}) − K, 0)\n52: 2. Up-and-out call, discrete monitoring: B(S) = max(S_T − K, 0) · 1{max(S_{t_1..m}) < B}\n53: 3. Digital call: D = 1{S_T > K}\n54: 4. European vanilla call (validation benchmark): E = max(S_T − K, 0)\n55: \n56: ### 3.3 Black–Scholes benchmark and validation duty\n57: \n58: European call: C_BS = S0·N(d1) − K e^{−rT} N(d2), d1,2 = [ln(S0/K) ± (r ± σ²/2)T]/(σ√T). Validation: z = (MC − C_BS)/SE_MC, PASS iff |z| ≤ 3. Reported in §4.1.\n59: \n60: ### 3.4 Geometric Asian control variate (exact discrete moments)\n61: \n62: For the same discrete grid, G = (Π S_{t_i})^{1/m} is lognormal with\n63: \n64: μ_G = ln S0 + (r − σ²/2)·T·(m+1)/(2m),   var_G = σ²T²·(m+1)(2m+1)/(6m²),\n65: \n66: E[G] = e^{μ_G + var_G/2}, and the geometric-Asian call price has the Black–Scholes-type closed form (d1 = (μ_G − ln K + var_G)/√var_G). The control-variate estimator for the arithmetic Asian call uses per-path geometric payoffs as the control with the closed-form geometric-Asian call as the reference expectation; β̂ = Ĉov(A,G)/V̂ar(G) estimated in-sample (asymptotically unbiased at N = 2^17).\n67: \n68: ### 3.5 Greeks\n69: \n70: * **Pathwise (valid only for a.s. differentiable payoffs):**\n71:   delta_vanilla = e^{−rT} E[1{S_T>K}·S_T/S0]; delta_asian = e^{−rT} E[1{A>K}·(1/m Σ S_i)/S0];\n72:   vega_asian = e^{−rT} E[1{A>K}·(1/m Σ S_i·(√t_i Z_i − σ t_i))].\n73: * **Central finite differences with common random numbers:** spot bump h ∈ {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}·S0; vega uses absolute vol bumps ε ∈ {0.1, 0.01, 0.001} (i.e. h/S0-scaled, documented). Common random numbers make the FD estimator's variance finite and its bias O(h²).\n74: * **Digital and barrier payoffs are discontinuous** ⇒ naive pathwise differentiation yields 0 a.s. (the indicator's derivative is a Dirac mass) and is *not* reported as an estimator; FD is reported instead, and the bias/variance tradeoff across h is analysed.\n75: * BS analytic delta (N(d1)) and vega (S0·√T·N′(d1)) reported for the vanilla as ground truth.\n76: \n77: ### 3.6 Convergence and verification protocol\n78: \n79: RMSE(N) over N ∈ {2^8,…,2^17}, R = 20 independent replications per N; log10–log10 fit of RMSE vs N; fitted slope compared against the theoretical −1/2 with its OLS standard error (assumption: independent replications; reported, not assumed). Antithetic halves the variance for positively-correlated monotone payoffs; control variate removes the geometric component of variance exactly.\n80: \n81: ### 3.7 Option B — deep hedging specification\n82: \n83: * Payoff: European vanilla call (cleanest analytic BS-delta benchmark).\n84: * Policy: Δ_i = f_θ(S_i/S0, t_i/T); MLP ≤ 3 hidden layers (64-64-64, ReLU, linear output). Decisions use only F_{t_i}.\n85: * Accounting (assignment formula, exact conventions): hedging grid t_i = i·dt, i = 0..m−1; Δ_i set at t_i;\n86:   V_T = Σ_i e^{r(T−t_i)} Δ_i (S_{i+1} − S_i) − κ Σ_i |Δ_i − Δ_{i−1}|·S_{t_i} − H(S_T),  Δ_{−1} := 0\n87:   (initial position charged; costs at decision-time spot; **no extra closeout term** — the final hedging P&L leg realises the last move).\n88: * Premium: **excluded** exactly as the assignment writes; adding the constant e^{rT}·C_BS would shift mean P&L (and CVaR) identically across all policies and leave the variance and all policy rankings unchanged.\n89: * Objective: L = −V_T; minimise empirical CVaR_0.95(L) in the Rockafellar–Uryasev form min_{θ,η} η + (1/(1−α))·mean(relu(L − η)), α = 0.95, η learnable. Out-of-sample CVaR evaluated directly (mean of worst 5%) independently of the training loss.\n90: * Training: N_train = 2^17 = 131072 simulated paths (seed 42); validation 2^15 paths (seed 123) with early stopping (patience 12); test 2^15 paths (seed 2026) never touched during training. Minibatches, Adam.\n91: * Benchmarks: BS delta Δ = N(d1(t,S)) with recomputed τ = T−t, at rebalancing frequencies {1, 5, 21} days and κ ∈ {0, 0.001, 0.005} (0/10/50 bp) — 9 combinations — plus the neural policy at the same three κ levels (every-step rebalancing). Metrics on test paths: E[V_T], Var(V_T), CVaR_0.95(−V_T), turnover Σ|ΔΔ|, mean cost per path.\n92: * The same accounting applies to neural and baseline policies (identical cost model, premium exclusion, discounting).\n93: \n94: ## 4. Results\n95: \n96: *[TO BE FILLED FROM results/approach1/if/metrics.json and results/approach2/if/metrics.json after the experiment runs; figures referenced from results/.]*\n97: \n98: ## 5. Discussion and limitations\n99: \n100: * GBM-with-drift is the assignment's model; real futures exhibit mean-reversion/jumps and the physical drift is negative in the sample — none of this enters the risk-neutral price.\n101: * Continuous main contract roll gaps; log-return mitigation; no back-adjustment.\n102: * Discrete monitoring (252/y) of barrier/average; continuous monitoring would change values (barrier especially; discrete is the assignment's spec).\n103: * Risk-neutral CVaR ≠ real-world market risk; deep-hedge advantage (if any) is relative to the simulator's measure and the vanilla call payoff.\n104: * SHIBOR 1Y flat for T=1Y; no dividend/convenience-yield modelling; futures basis not modelled (assignment prescribes GBM on the futures level).\n105: * Asian/barrier Greeks by FD have O(h²) bias; pathwise invalid there.\n106: * Neural results hold only out-of-sample (test seed 2026); in-sample training fit is not evidence of hedging skill.\n107: \n108: ## 6.
